Makkī (Meccan) is this surah.

{1} This is information about His praise and commendation, by His attributes of perfection and His qualities of greatness and majesty, in general, and in particular concerning what is mentioned here. He praised Himself for creating the heavens and the earth, which indicate the perfection of His power, the vastness of His knowledge and mercy, the all-encompassing scope of His wisdom, and His sole authority over creation and governance; and for making the darknesses and the light. This includes the perceptible kinds of these, such as night and day, the sun and the moon, and the immaterial kinds, such as the darknesses of ignorance, doubt, polytheism, disobedience and heedlessness, and the light of knowledge, faith, certainty and obedience. All of this proves decisively that He, Exalted is He, is the one deserving of worship and of sincere devotion in religion. Despite this proof and the clarity of the evidence, ﴿yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾; [i.e., they ascribe equals] to Him other than Him, making them equal to Him in worship and veneration, even though they are not equal to Allah in any aspect of perfection, and they are poor, powerless, and deficient in every respect.

{2} ﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾: by creating your substance and your father Adam (peace be upon him). ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾; i.e., He set a term for the duration of your residence in this abode, during which you enjoy its benefits, are tested, and are afflicted by what His messengers bring to them, ﴿that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾, and He grants you a lifespan in which whoever will be mindful remembers. ﴿And there is a specified term with Him﴾: this is the Hereafter, to which the servants transfer from this abode, where He will recompense them for their deeds, good or evil. ﴿Yet you doubt﴾; i.e., despite this complete clarification and the establishment of proof, you doubt the promise and threat of Allah and the occurrence of recompense on the Day of Resurrection.

Allah mentioned the "darknesses" in the plural because of the multiplicity of their sources and the variety of their paths, and He mentioned "the light" in the singular because the path leading to Allah is one, with no multiplicity in it; it is the path that includes knowledge of the truth and acting upon it, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And that this is My path, [which is] straight, so follow it. And do not follow [other] ways, for they will separate you from His way﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verse 4–6:

{4} This is a report from Him, exalted is He, concerning the aversion of the polytheists, the severity of their denial and their enmity, and that signs do not benefit them until calamities (al-mathulat) befall them. So He said: ﴿And there does not come to them any sign from the signs of their Lord﴾ that indicates the truth with decisive proof, calling them to follow and accept it, ﴿except that they were turning away from it﴾: they pay no attention to it and do not lend it their ears, their hearts having turned toward other things, and they have turned their backs on it.

{5} ﴿So they have denied the truth when it came to them﴾. The truth's due is that it be followed, and that God be thanked for facilitating it for them and bringing it to them. Yet they met it with the opposite of what it required, so they deserved severe punishment. ﴿So there will come to them the news of that which they used to mock﴾; that is, they will soon see that what they mocked is the truth and the reality, and God will make clear to the deniers their lying and fabrication. They used to mock the resurrection, Paradise and Hell. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said to the deniers: "This is the Fire which you used to deny." And God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they swore by God their most emphatic oaths that God would not resurrect those who die. Yes, [it is] a promise binding upon Him, true, but most of the people do not know. [He will resurrect them] to make clear to them that wherein they differ, and that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars﴾.

{6} Then He commanded them to take heed from the earlier nations, so He said: ﴿Did they not see how many generations We destroyed before them?﴾; that is, how many successive destructions We brought upon the nations who denied, and We gave them respite before that destruction, [by] ﴿establishing them upon the earth as We have not established you﴾ in wealth, children and affluence. ﴿And We sent down the sky upon them in abundant rain and made rivers flow beneath them﴾: thereby causing to grow for them whatever God willed of crops and fruits, which they enjoyed and from which they took whatever they desired. Yet they did not thank God for His blessings; rather, they devoted themselves to desires, and [various] pleasures diverted them. Then their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they did not believe them; rather, they rejected and denied them, so God destroyed them for their sins and brought forth after them another generation. This is the custom of God and His way with the earlier and later nations. So take heed from those whose stories God has related to you.

{7} This is an announcement from God to His Messenger about the extreme obstinacy of the disbelievers, and that their denial is not due to any deficiency in what you brought them, nor to any ignorance on their part of it; rather, that is injustice and transgression, for which there is no remedy on your part. So He said: ﴿And if We had sent down to you a written scroll on paper, and they had touched it with their hands﴾: and been certain of it, ﴿the disbelievers would have said: "This is nothing but clear magic."﴾ Out of injustice and arrogance. So what clearer proof is there than this proof? And this is their shameful statement about it, in that they denied what is perceptible to the senses, which no one with even the least portion of intellect can repel!

{8} ﴿And they said﴾ also, out of obstinacy, based on ignorance and lack of knowledge of what is rational: ﴿"Why has not an angel been sent down to him?"﴾; that is: why was an angel not sent down with Muhammad to assist him and support him in what he is upon, according to their claim that he is a human being and that the message of God can only come through the hands of angels. God stated, in explaining His mercy and kindness toward His servants, that He sent to them a human being from among them, so that belief in what he brought would come from knowledge, insight, and the unseen: ﴿And if We had sent down an angel﴾ with Our message, ﴿the matter would have been decided﴾: by hastening the destruction upon them and not granting them respite; because this is God's custom regarding those who ask for proposed signs and then do not believe in them. Therefore, sending a human messenger to them with clear signs, which God knows to be more beneficial and gentler for the servants, along with God's granting respite to the disbelievers and deniers, is better and more useful for them; so their request for the sending down of an angel is an evil for them, if only they knew.

{9} Moreover, even if an angel were sent down to them and dispatched, they would not be able to receive from him, nor could they bear that, nor could their perishable powers endure it. So, ﴿if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man﴾: because wisdom requires nothing other than that, ﴿and We would have confused them as they now confuse themselves﴾; that is: the matter would have been mixed up and obscured for them, and that is due to what they had obscured for themselves. For they built their affair upon this principle, which contains confusion and the absence of clarifying the truth. When the truth came to them by its correct paths and its rules, which are its own rules, it was not guidance for them, even though others were guided by it; the fault is theirs, since they shut the door of guidance upon themselves and opened the doors of misguidance.

{11} If you doubt that or are uncertain of it, ﴿then travel through the earth and see what was the end of the deniers.﴾ You will find only peoples who were destroyed, and nations who perished as examples, whose dwellings have become desolate and whose abodes have been emptied of every joyful one who once enjoyed delight. Allah says to His Prophet (ﷺ): {Say}, to these polytheists who associate others with Allah, establishing the point against them and binding them to tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness): {To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?}; that is, who is the Creator of that, the Owner of it, and the One who disposes of it? {Say}, to them: {To Allah}. They acknowledge this and do not deny it. So when they have acknowledged that Allah alone possesses the dominion and the management, should they not also acknowledge that He alone deserves sincere devotion and tawhid?

And His saying: {He has prescribed for Himself mercy}; that is, the upper and lower worlds are under His dominion and management. He has spread His mercy and kindness over them, and enveloped them with His mercy and bounty. He has prescribed for Himself a decree: that His mercy overcomes His wrath, that giving is more beloved to Him than withholding, and that Allah has opened the doors of mercy to all of His servants, unless they close those doors upon themselves through their sins; and He calls them to it, unless their acts of disobedience and their defects prevent them from seeking it.

And His saying: {He will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt}. This is an oath from Him, and He is the most truthful of those who inform. He has established for this such proofs and evidences as make it certain truth (haqq al-yaqin). But the wrongdoers refused except to deny, and they rejected Allah's power to resurrect the creation. So they hastened into His disobedience and became bold in disbelief in Him, and they lost both their worldly life and their Hereafter. For this reason He said: {Those who have lost their souls, for they do not believe}.

Know that this noble surah includes the establishment of tawhid by every rational and textual proof; indeed, nearly all of it concerns tawhid and the disputation with the polytheists who associate others with Allah and who deny His Messenger. In these verses, Allah has mentioned that by which guidance becomes clear and by which shirk is suppressed:

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verses 13–20:**

{13} He mentions that ﴿to Him belongs whatever dwells in the night and the day﴾. This includes all created beings: humans, jinn, angels, animals and inanimate things. All of them are creatures, managed and subjected, servants compelled to serve their mighty, dominant and sovereign Lord. Can it be valid by reason and by revelation to worship any of these subjects, who possess neither benefit nor harm, while sincerity is abandoned toward the Creator, the Manager, the Sovereign who harms and benefits? Or do sound minds and upright natural dispositions (fitrah) call to sincere worship, love, fear and hope directed to God, the Lord of the worlds? ﴿As-Sami'﴾: He hears all voices across the differences of languages and the variety of needs. ﴿Al-'Alim﴾: He knows what has been, what will be, and what has not been, and how it would have been had it been. He is aware of the outward and the inward.

{14} Say, ﴿Shall I take as a protector other than God?﴾ That is, from these weak creatures, who would support and help me? I do not take any protector besides Him, because He is ﴿the Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, their Creator and Manager, ﴿and He feeds but is not fed﴾, that is, He is the Provider of all creation without any need on His part for them. How then would it be fitting for me to take as a protector anyone other than the Creator, the Provider, the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy? ﴿Say: Indeed I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit﴾ to God in monotheism and to yield to Him in obedience, because I am more entitled than others to carry out the commands of my Lord. ﴿And never be of the polytheists﴾: that is, I have also been forbidden from being among the polytheists, neither in their belief, nor in sitting with them, nor in gathering with them. This is the most obligatory of obligations upon me and the most binding of duties.

{15} ﴿Say: Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day﴾, for disobedience in the form of polytheism requires eternal abiding in the Fire and the wrath of the Almighty.

{16} That day is the day whose punishment is feared and whose retribution is dreaded. Whoever is turned away from punishment on that day is the one who has been shown mercy, and whoever is saved on it is truly the successful one, just as whoever is not saved from it is the ruined and wretched one.

{17} Among the proofs of His oneness is that He alone removes harm and brings about good and ease. For this reason He said: ﴿If God touches you with harm﴾, such as poverty, sickness, hardship, grief, anxiety or the like, ﴿there is no remover of it except Him. And if He touches you with good, then He is over all things competent﴾. So when He alone is the one who benefits and harms, He is the one who deserves to be singled out for worship and divinity.

{18} ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants﴾. No one among them acts, no mover moves, and no still thing rests except by His will. Neither kings nor others can step outside His dominion and authority. Rather, they are all managed and subjugated. So when He is the Subduer and others are subjugated, He is the one who deserves to be worshipped. ﴿And He is the Wise﴾ in what He commands and forbids, in what He rewards and punishes, and in what He creates and decrees. ﴿The Acquainted﴾: He is aware of hidden secrets, inner thoughts and concealed matters. All of this is among the proofs of monotheism (tawhid).

{19} Say, to them, after We have made the guidance clear to them and explained the paths to them: ﴿What thing is greatest in testimony?﴾ concerning this great principle. Say: ﴿God is the greatest in testimony. He is a witness between me and you﴾. There is no greater or more mighty testimony than His, and He bears witness for me by His affirmation and His action. He confirms me in what I have told you, as He said: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings, We would have seized him by the right hand and then severed from him the aorta﴾. God is Wise and Able, so it is not befitting His wisdom and power to confirm one who lies against Him, claiming that God sent him when He did not send him, that God commanded him to call the people when He did not command him, and that God permitted him the blood, wealth and women of those who oppose him. Yet He still affirms him by His approval and His action, supporting him in what he says with overwhelming miracles and manifest signs, granting him victory, and humiliating those who oppose and oppose him. What testimony is greater than this testimony? As for His saying: ﴿And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches﴾, that is, God revealed to me this noble Qur'an for your benefit and welfare, so that I may warn you of painful punishment. Warning is only achieved by mentioning what warns them of, through encouragement and intimidation, and by explaining the outward and inward deeds and statements, such that whoever acts upon them has accepted the warning. So this Qur'an contains warning for you, O addressees, and for everyone the Qur'an reaches until the Day of Resurrection, for it contains the explanation of everything needed in the divine matters.

When He, the Exalted, had made clear His testimony, which is the greatest of testimonies to His oneness, He said: Say to those who oppose God's report and deny His messengers: ﴿Do you indeed testify that there are other gods with God?﴾ Say: ﴿I do not testify﴾. That is, if they testify, then do not testify along with them. {25} That is: among these polytheists there are people whom, at certain times, some motives move to listen [to what you say], but it is a listening devoid of seeking the truth and following it. For this reason they do not benefit from that listening, since they do not desire good. ﴿And We have placed coverings over their hearts﴾; that is, coverings and veils, so that they do not comprehend the speech of Allah, and so He protects His speech from the likes of these people. ﴿And in their ears﴾ We have placed ﴿deafness﴾; that is, deafness, so they do not listen to what would benefit them. ﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it﴾: this is the utmost of injustice and obstinacy, that the clear signs which indicate the truth they neither submit to nor affirm, but rather they dispute the truth with falsehood in order to refute it. For this reason He said: ﴿until, when they come to you disputing with you, those who disbelieve say, "This is nothing but the myths of the former peoples."﴾ That is: taken from the written scriptures of the ancients, which are not from Allah nor from His messengers. This is from their disbelief. Otherwise, how could this Book, which contains the reports of those before and after, and the realities brought by the prophets and messengers, and the truth, the justice and the complete equity in every respect, be the myths of the ancients?!

{26} {And they} — that is, the polytheists who associate others with Allah and deny His Messenger — combine going astray with leading others astray. They forbid people from following the truth and warn them against it, and they keep themselves far from it. Yet by this conduct they will not harm Allah or His believing servants in the slightest. ﴿They destroy none but themselves, and they do not perceive it.﴾ That is, they are unaware of it.

{30} That is: {And if you could see} the disbelievers {when they are made to stand before their Lord}; you would see a great matter and a mighty terror. {He will say} to them, rebuking and reproaching them: {"Is this not the truth?"} — the punishment you are seeing. {They will say, "Yes, by our Lord!"} — so they acknowledge and confess, at a time when that does not benefit them. {He will say, "Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve."}

{31} That is: Those who denied the meeting with Allah have indeed lost, been ruined, and been deprived of all good. This denial necessitated for them audacity toward the forbidden and committing of the destructive sins. {Until, when the Hour comes upon them} while they are in the worst and most wretched state, {they will say, "Oh, our regret over what we neglected concerning it!"} and they show the utmost remorse. But this regret is a lament whose time has passed. {And they will carry their burdens upon their backs. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear} for their burden is a load that weighs them down and from which they cannot free themselves. For this reason they are abided forever in the Fire, and they deserve eternity in the wrath of the All-Powerful.

{32} This is the reality of the worldly life and the reality of the Hereafter. As for the reality of the worldly life, it is play and amusement: play for the bodies, and amusement for the hearts. The hearts are bewildered by it, the souls are enamored of it, and worries are attached to it, and occupation with it is like the play of children. As for the Hereafter, it is ﴿better for those who fear God﴾, in its essence and its attributes, and in its permanence and its everlastingness. In it is what the souls desire and what the eyes find delight in, of the bliss of the hearts and spirits, and abundant joy and happiness. But it is not for everyone; it is only for those who fear God (al-muttaqun), who carry out the commands of God and abandon His prohibitions and deterrents. ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾ That is: will you not have intellects by which you perceive which of the two abodes is more deserving of being preferred?

{33} That is: We know that what the deniers say about you grieves you and distresses you, and We did not command you with what We commanded you of patience except so that you might attain lofty ranks and noble states. So do not think that their saying arises from confusion about your affair or doubt concerning you: {Indeed, they do not deny you} — because they know your truthfulness, your entry and your exit, and all your conditions, to the extent that they used to call him, before his prophethood, "the Trustworthy" (al-Amin). {But the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah} — that is, their denial is of the signs of Allah which Allah placed at your hands.

{34} {And messengers were denied before you, and they were patient over what they were denied and harmed, until Our help came to them}: So be patient as they were patient, and you will prevail as they prevailed. {And there has certainly come to you from the news of the messengers} — that by which your heart is made firm and your breast is reassured.

{35} {And if their turning away has been difficult for you}: that is, it has weighed heavily upon you because of your eagerness for them and your love for their faith. So exert your utmost effort in that, but it is not within your power to guide whom Allah does not will to guide. {So if you are able to seek a tunnel into the earth or a ladder into the sky and bring them a sign} — that is, then do that, for it will benefit them nothing; and this is a cutting off of his hope for the guidance of such stubborn opponents. {And if Allah had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance}: but His wisdom, may He be exalted, required that they remain in misguidance. {So do not be among the ignorant} — those who do not know the realities of matters nor place them in their proper stations.

**(36)** Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Only those who hear﴾ your call, answer your message, and submit to your command and prohibition, will respond. ﴿Those who hear﴾ with their hearts what benefits them, and they are the people of intellect and hearing. The hearing meant here is the hearing of the heart and the acceptance it brings. Otherwise, mere hearing by the ear is shared by the righteous and the wicked, since every person under obligation has been confronted with Allah's proof through hearing His verses, so they have no excuse for not accepting. ﴿And the dead, Allah will raise them; then to Him they will be returned.﴾ It is possible that this meaning is the opposite of what was mentioned: that is, only the living of heart will respond to you. As for the dead of heart, who do not perceive their happiness and do not sense what would save them, they will not respond to you or submit. Their appointed time is the Resurrection, when Allah will raise them, and then to Him they will be returned. It is also possible that the verse is meant in its apparent sense: that Allah establishes the return (to Him), that He will raise the dead on the Day of Resurrection, and then inform them of what they used to do. This would contain both an encouragement to respond to Allah and His Messenger, and a warning against not doing so.

**(37)** ﴿And they said﴾, meaning the deniers of the Messenger, out of obstinacy and stubbornness: ﴿Why has not a sign been sent down upon him from his Lord?﴾ By this they mean the demanded signs, which they propose by their corrupt minds and worthless opinions, such as their saying: ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth. Or you will have a garden of palm trees and grapevines and cause rivers to gush forth within them in abundance. Or you will cause the sky to fall upon us in fragments, as you claim, or bring Allah and the angels before us as a guarantee..."﴾ and the rest of the verses. ﴿Say﴾, responding to their statement: ﴿Indeed, Allah is able to send down a sign﴾. There is no deficiency in His power to do so, how not, when all things are subject to His might and submissive to His authority? But most of the people do not know. Due to their ignorance and lack of knowledge, they seek what is worse for them among the signs; if such signs came to them and they still did not believe, they would have been hastened to punishment, as is the unchanging way of Allah. ﴿And there is no creature on earth, nor bird that flies with its wings, but they are communities like you. We have not neglected in the Book anything. Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾ (38). Despite this, if their intention is the signs that clarify the truth and make the path evident, then Muhammad (ﷺ) has brought every decisive sign and clear proof indicating the truth he brought, such that in every matter of religion the servant can find in what he brought several rational and traditional proofs, leaving no slightest doubt or suspicion in the hearts. Blessed is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth, and supported him with clear signs, so that whoever perishes may perish with clear proof, and whoever lives may live with clear proof. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.

{38} That is: all the land animals and the flying creatures, the beasts, the wild animals and the birds, are communities like you. We created them as We created you, and We provided for them as We provided for you, and Our will and Our power have taken effect upon them just as they have taken effect upon you. ﴿We have not neglected anything in the Book﴾; that is, We have not overlooked or omitted anything in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). Rather, all things, small and great, are recorded in the Preserved Tablet as they are, so every event occurs exactly in accordance with what the Pen has written. In this verse there is evidence that the first Book encompasses all created beings. This is one of the levels of qada' and qadar (divine decree and predestination), for they are four levels: the knowledge of Allah, which comprehends all things; His Book, which encompasses all existing things; His will and power, which take effect generally over everything; and His creation of all created things, including the actions of the servants. It is also possible that the intended "Book" here is this Qur'an, and that the meaning is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We have sent down to you the Book as an exposition of all things﴾. And His saying: ﴿Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾; that is, all the communities will be brought together and assembled before Allah at the standing of the Resurrection, in that great and terrifying standing, where He will recompense them with His justice and His kindness, and carry out upon them His judgment, which the first and the last, the people of the heavens and the people of the earth, will praise Him for.

{39} This is an explanation of the state of those who deny the signs of God and deny His messengers: they have closed for themselves the door of guidance and opened the door of perdition, and they are {deaf} to hearing the truth, {dumb} from speaking it, so they speak only falsehood, {in darknesses}; that is, they are immersed in the darknesses of ignorance, disbelief, wrongdoing, obstinacy and sins. This is from God's misguiding them, for {whomever God wills, He leaves astray, and whomever He wills, He places upon a straight path} (Qur'an 6:39), because He alone is the One who solely possesses guidance and misguidance, according to what His grace and wisdom require.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 6, verses 40–41:**

{40} Almighty Allah says to His Messenger: {Say} to the polytheists who associate others with Allah and equate others with Him: {Tell me, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you, or the Hour comes upon you, would you call upon other than Allah, if you are truthful?} That is: if these hardships and these distresses, from which one is compelled to seek relief, befall you, will you call upon your gods and your idols, or will you call upon your Lord, the King, the Manifest Truth?

{41} {Rather, it is Him you call upon, and He removes what you call upon Him for, if He wills, and you forget what you associate with Him.} That is: if this is your condition with your rivals in times of severe trial, you forget them, knowing that they possess no power to benefit or harm you, nor power over death, life, or resurrection, and you sincerely devote your supplication to Allah, knowing that He is the One who harms and benefits, the One who responds to the supplication of the one in distress. Then how is it that in ease you associate others with Him and make for Him partners? Has reason or transmitted revelation guided you to this? Or do you have any authority for this? Or do you attribute falsehood to Allah?

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verses 42–45:

{42} He, exalted is He, says: {And We certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you}: [to] the nations of the past and the generations gone before, so they denied Our messengers and rejected Our signs. {Then We seized them with adversity and hardship}; that is, with poverty, sickness, afflictions and calamities, out of mercy from Us toward them, {so that they might humble themselves}, before Us, and turn to Us in supplication when hardship befalls them.

{43} {Why, when Our punishment came upon them, did they not humble themselves? But their hearts were hardened}; that is, they became like stone, not softening to the truth. {And Satan made attractive to them what they were doing}: so they supposed that what they were upon was the religion of truth, and they enjoyed their falsehood for a time, and Satan played with their minds.

{44} {So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened to them the gates of everything}: [the gates] of this world, its pleasures and its heedlessness, {until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly, and they were then in despair}; that is, hopeless of every good. This is the most severe form of punishment: that they be seized unawares, heedless and at ease, so that it may be more intense for their punishment and greater for their calamity.

{45} {So the last of the people who did wrong were cut off}; that is, they were completely uprooted by the punishment, and their means were severed from them. {And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds}: for what He decreed and destined of the destruction of the deniers; for through that His signs are made clear, His honouring of His friends and His humiliating of His enemies, and the truth of what the messengers brought become evident.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verses 46–47:

{46} He, may He be exalted, informs that just as He alone creates things and manages them, He alone is singular in Oneness (tawhid) and divinity (uluhiyyah). So He says: Say, "Tell me, if Allah took away your hearing and your sight and sealed over your hearts," [then you would be left without hearing, sight, or understanding]. "Who is a god other than Allah who could bring them back to you?" So if none other than Allah can bring that about, why do you worship alongside Him one who has no power over anything unless Allah wills it? This is among the proofs of tawhid and of the invalidity of shirk. For this reason He says: {Look how We vary the signs}, that is, We diversify them and bring them in every kind of form, so that the truth may be made clear and the way of the criminals may become evident. {Yet they turn away} despite this complete clarification, {turning aside} from the signs of Allah and refusing them.

{47} {Say, "Tell me"}, that is, inform me: {if the punishment of Allah comes upon you suddenly or openly}, that is, unexpectedly, or preceded by signs by which you know it is coming, {will any be destroyed except the wrongdoing people}: those who became the cause of the punishment befalling them through their wrongdoing and obstinacy. So beware of persisting in wrongdoing, for it leads to everlasting destruction and endless wretchedness.

{48} Exalted is He, mentions the essence of what He sent the messengers with: that it is good tidings (al-bishara) and warning (al-nidhara). This necessarily entails an explanation of: the bearer of good tidings, the one who receives them, the good tidings themselves, and the deeds which, when a servant performs them, bring him the good tidings; and the warner, the one warned, the thing he is warned of, and the deeds which, when a person does them, make the warning binding upon him. However, people divided into two categories according to their response to their call and their lack of response:

﴿Whoever believes and does righteous deeds﴾; that is, believes in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, and makes his faith, his deeds, and his intention sound. ﴿There will be no fear for them﴾: regarding what is yet to come, ﴿nor will they grieve﴾: over what has passed.

Ibn Sa'di's commentary (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 6, verse 50:

{50} Almighty God says to His Prophet ﷺ, addressing those who asked him for signs, or who said to him, "You only call us so that we take you as a god besides God": ﴿Say: I do not tell you that I have the treasuries of God﴾; that is, the keys to His provision and His mercy. ﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾: all of that is with God alone. He is the One who, whatever mercy He opens for people, none can withhold, and whatever He withholds, none can release after Him. He alone knows the unseen and the seen, and He does not reveal His unseen to anyone except a messenger whom He has chosen. ﴿Nor do I tell you that I am an angel﴾: so that I could act with unrestricted power and strength. I do not claim beyond the station to which God has raised me. ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me﴾; that is, this is my goal, the limit and the highest of my affair: I only follow what is revealed to me, acting upon it in myself and calling all of creation to it. So when my station is known, for what purpose does the seeker investigate with me, or ask of me a matter that I do not claim? Can a person be obligated to what is not his concern? Ibn Sa'di's commentary (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 6, verses 56–58:

{56} Allah says to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾ to these polytheists who call upon other gods besides Allah: ﴿Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those whom you call upon besides Allah﴾, from among the rivals and idols, which possess no benefit, no harm, no causing of death, no giving of life, and no resurrection. This is falsehood, and you have no proof or even a doubt in it, except following desire, and following desire is the greatest misguidance. For this reason He said: ﴿Say: I will not follow your desires; I would then have strayed, and I would not be among the rightly guided﴾; that is, if I followed your desires, ﴿and I would not be among the rightly guided﴾ in any way whatsoever.

{57} As for what I am upon of the tawhid of Allah and sincerity of deed toward Him, it is the truth, upon which stand the proofs and decisive evidences, and I am ﴿upon clear evidence from my Lord﴾; that is, upon a manifest certainty of its soundness and the falsehood of whatever is other than it. This is a firm testimony from the Messenger that admits of no hesitation, and he is the most just of witnesses [among creation] absolutely. The believers affirmed it, and its soundness and truthfulness became clear to them according to what Allah bestowed upon them, but you, O polytheists, ﴿have denied it﴾, and it does not deserve this from you, nor is anything befitting of it but affirmation. And if you persist in your denial, then know that the punishment will certainly befall you, and it is with Allah; He sends it down upon you when He wills and as He wills. And if you hasten it, then the matter is not in my hand at all. ﴿Judgment belongs only to Allah﴾. Just as He is the One who issued the legislative judgment, commanding and forbidding, He will issue the judgment of recompense, rewarding and punishing according to what His wisdom requires. So objection to His judgment in any form is rejected. He has made the path clear and related the truth to His servants in a manner that cut off their excuses and ended their argument, so that whoever perishes perishes after clear evidence, and whoever lives lives after clear evidence. ﴿And He is the best of judges﴾ among His servants in this world and the Hereafter, so He decides between them with a decision for which He is praised, even by the one against whom it is issued and to whom the truth is turned.

{58} ﴿Say﴾ to those who hasten the punishment out of ignorance, obstinacy and injustice: ﴿If I had what you are hastening for, the matter would have been decided between me and you﴾; I would have brought it upon you, and there would be no good for you in that. But the matter is with the Forbearing, the Patient, who is disobeyed by the disobedient and dared against by the audacious, yet He pardons them, provides for them, and bestows upon them His outward and inward blessings. ﴿And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers﴾; nothing of their conditions is hidden from Him, so He gives them respite and does not neglect them.

{56} Allah says to His Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾ to these polytheists who call upon other gods besides Allah: ﴿Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those whom you call upon besides Allah﴾, from among the rivals and idols, which possess no benefit, no harm, no causing of death, no giving of life, and no resurrection. This is falsehood, and you have no proof or even a doubt in it, except following desire, and following desire is the greatest misguidance. For this reason He said: ﴿Say: I will not follow your desires; I would then have strayed, and I would not be among the rightly guided﴾; that is, if I followed your desires, ﴿and I would not be among the rightly guided﴾ in any way whatsoever.

{57} As for what I am upon of the tawhid of Allah and sincerity of deed toward Him, it is the truth, upon which stand the proofs and decisive evidences, and I am ﴿upon clear evidence from my Lord﴾; that is, upon a manifest certainty of its soundness and the falsehood of whatever is other than it. This is a firm testimony from the Messenger that admits of no hesitation, and he is the most just of witnesses [among creation] absolutely. The believers affirmed it, and its soundness and truthfulness became clear to them according to what Allah bestowed upon them, but you, O polytheists, ﴿have denied it﴾, and it does not deserve this from you, nor is anything befitting of it but affirmation. And if you persist in your denial, then know that the punishment will certainly befall you, and it is with Allah; He sends it down upon you when He wills and as He wills. And if you hasten it, then the matter is not in my hand at all. ﴿Judgment belongs only to Allah﴾. Just as He is the One who issued the legislative judgment, commanding and forbidding, He will issue the judgment of recompense, rewarding and punishing according to what His wisdom requires. So objection to His judgment in any form is rejected. He has made the path clear and related the truth to His servants in a manner that cut off their excuses and ended their argument, so that whoever perishes perishes after clear evidence, and whoever lives lives after clear evidence. ﴿And He is the best of judges﴾ among His servants in this world and the Hereafter, so He decides between them with a decision for which He is praised, even by the one against whom it is issued and to whom the truth is turned.

{58} ﴿Say﴾ to those who hasten the punishment out of ignorance, obstinacy and injustice: ﴿If I had what you are hastening for, the matter would have been decided between me and you﴾; I would have brought it upon you, and there would be no good for you in that. But the matter is with the Forbearing, the Patient, who is disobeyed by the disobedient and dared against by the audacious, yet He pardons them, provides for them, and bestows upon them His outward and inward blessings. ﴿And Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers﴾; nothing of their conditions is hidden from Him, so He gives them respite and does not neglect them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verse 59:

{59} This great verse is among the greatest in detailing His all-encompassing knowledge, and that it comprises all the unseen matters, of which He reveals whatever He wills to His creation, while He has kept much of His knowledge hidden from the nearest angels and the messenger prophets, not to mention others among the worlds. It also includes His knowledge of what is in the deserts and wastelands: the animals, the trees, the sands, the pebbles, and the dust; and what is in the seas: their animals, their minerals, their game, and other things that their expanses contain and their waters enclose. {And not a leaf falls}: from the trees of the land and the sea, in the towns and the wastelands, in this world and the Hereafter, except that He knows it. {Nor is there a grain in the darknesses of the earth}: from the grains of fruits and crops, and the seeds that people sow, and the seeds of wild plants from which various kinds of vegetation grow. {Nor anything fresh or dry}: this is a generality after a specification. {Except that it is in a clear Book}: and this is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz); it has encompassed them and comprises them. Some of what is mentioned here dazzles the intellects of the wise and bewilders the hearts of the noble. This indicates the greatness of the Mighty Lord and His vastness in all His attributes, and that the creation, from first to last, if they gathered together to encompass even some of His attributes, would have no power or capacity to do so. Blessed is the Mighty, the Vast, the All-Knowing, the Praiseworthy, the Glorious, the Witness, the All-Encompassing Lord, and exalted is a God whom no one can count the praises of; rather He is as He has praised Himself, and beyond what His servants praise Him. This verse therefore indicates His all-encompassing knowledge of all things and His Book encompassing all events.

All of this is an affirmation of His divinity and an argument against the polytheists concerning it, and an explanation that He, exalted is He, is the one deserving of love, exaltation, reverence, and honor.

{60} He informed that He alone is the One who exclusively manages His servants in their wakefulness and their sleep. He takes them in death at night, the death of sleep, so their movements become still and their bodies rest, and He returns them to wakefulness from their sleep so that they may conduct their religious and worldly affairs. He, exalted is He, knows what they have committed (jaraḥū) and earned (kasabū) of those deeds. Then He continues to manage them in this manner until they fulfil their terms (ājāl), so by this management there is a specified term (ajal musamma), which is the term of life, and another term after that, which is resurrection after death. For this reason He said: ﴿Then to Him is your return﴾: not to anyone else; ﴿then He will inform you of what you used to do﴾: of good and evil.

{61} ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants﴾: He executes over them His all-encompassing will and His general purpose. They possess nothing of the matter, and they neither move nor rest except by His permission. Yet He has appointed over the servants guardian angels (ḥafaẓah) who guard the servant and record what he does, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But indeed, over you are guardians, noble writers, who know what you do﴾ and ﴿[There are two] on the right and on the left, sitting [and recording]. He does not utter a word except that with him is an observer ready [to record]﴾. This is His guarding of them during life. ﴿Until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him﴾; i.e., the angels charged with seizing souls, ﴿and they do not neglect [their duty]﴾ in that; they do not add an hour to what Allah has decreed and determined, nor do they reduce it, and they execute nothing of that except according to the divine commands and the Lord's decrees.

{62} ﴿Then﴾: after death and the intermediate life (al-barzakh) and what is in it of good and evil, ﴿they are returned to Allah, their true Master﴾; i.e., the One who has taken charge of them by His decreed judgement, so He executed over them what He willed of the kinds of management; then He took charge of them by His command and prohibition, sent to them the messengers and sent down to them the books; then they are returned to Him so that He may exercise judgement over them by recompense, rewarding them for the good deeds they did and punishing them for evil deeds and misdeeds. For this reason He said: ﴿Unquestionably, to Him belongs judgement﴾: alone, with no partner, ﴿and He is the swiftest of reckoners﴾: because of the perfection of His knowledge and His preservation of their deeds, by what He recorded in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawḥ al-maḥfūz), and then His angels recorded it in the book that is in their hands.

So if He, exalted is He, is the One who alone creates and manages, and He is the Subduer over His servants, and He has cared for them with complete care in all their conditions, and to Him belong the decreed judgement, the legislated judgement and the judgement of recompense, then where is the excuse for the polytheists to turn away from the One described and characterised thus, to worship one who has no share in the matter, does not possess an atom's weight of benefit, and has no power or will? By Allah, if only they knew Allah's forbearance towards them, His pardon and His mercy toward them, while they oppose Him with polytheism and disbelief, and dare against His majesty with falsehood and slander, yet He grants them well-being and provision, their aspirations would have been drawn to knowing Him, their minds would have been dazed in His love, and they would have loathed themselves with the utmost loathing, for having submitted to the call of Satan, which entails disgrace and loss. But they are a people who do not reason.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verses 63–64:

{63} That is, {Say}, to the polytheists who call upon other deities besides Allah, holding them to what they themselves affirmed of Tawhid al-Rububiyyah (the Oneness of Lordship) in order to refute what they denied of Tawhid al-Uluhiyyah (the Oneness of Divinity): {Who rescues you from the darknesses of the land and the sea}; that is, from their severities and hardships, when the way out becomes impossible or difficult for you, so that you call upon your Lord humbly, with a submissive heart and a tongue that never ceases to beseech Him for your need in supplication, and you say, while in that state: {If He rescues us from this}: the distress into which we have fallen, {we will surely be among the thankful}: to Allah; that is, those who acknowledge His favor, who place it in obedience to their Lord, and who guard it from being spent in disobedience to Him.

{64} {Say, "Allah rescues you from it and from every affliction"}; that is, from this particular distress and from all general afflictions, {then you associate others with Him}: you do not fulfill to Allah what you have said, and you forget His favors upon you. So what proof could be clearer than this for the falsehood of shirk and the soundness of Tawhid?

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verses 68–69:

{68} What is meant by "immersing oneself in the verses of Allah" (al-khawd fi ayat Allah) is speaking in a way that contradicts the truth: embellishing false statements and calling to them, praising their proponents, turning away from the truth, and disparaging it and its people. Thus Allah commanded His Messenger primarily, and his community by extension, that when they see someone immersing himself in the verses of Allah in any of the ways mentioned, they should turn away from such people, not attend the gatherings of those who immerse themselves in falsehood, and persist in this until the discussion and immersion turn to other speech. When it turns to other speech, the aforementioned prohibition is lifted. If that is beneficial, it is commanded; if not, it is neither beneficial nor commanded. In the condemnation of immersing oneself in falsehood there is an exhortation to inquiry, reflection, and debate with the truth.

Then He said: {And if Satan causes you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people}: that is, by sitting with them in forgetfulness and heedlessness. It encompasses those who immerse themselves in falsehood and every speaker of what is forbidden or doer of what is forbidden, for it is unlawful to sit and be present when a wrong that one cannot remove is occurring. This prohibition and prohibition-by-ruling applies to one who sits with them and does not exercise taqwa of Allah, such as one who joins them in the forbidden speech or action, or remains silent about them and does not denounce them. But if he exercises taqwa of Allah, by commanding them to good and forbidding them from evil and from the speech that proceeds from them, and this results in the removal or lessening of the evil, then there is no blame or sin upon him. For this reason He said:

{69} {And upon those who fear Allah there is nothing of their reckoning, but a reminder, that perhaps they may fear Allah}: that is, but (it is incumbent) that he remind and admonish them, that perhaps they may fear Allah the Exalted. In this there is evidence that the one who reminds should use the speech most likely to achieve the intended goal of taqwa. There is also evidence that if reminding and admonishing would increase the one admonished in evil beyond his evil, then abandoning it is obligatory, because if it contradicts the intended purpose, then abandoning it becomes the intended purpose.

There is also evidence that if reminding and admonishing would increase the one admonished in evil beyond his evil, then abandoning it is obligatory, because if it contradicts the intended purpose, then abandoning it becomes the intended purpose.

{70} The purpose for which servants were created is that they should devote their religion sincerely to God, by worshipping Him alone with no partner, and by exerting their utmost ability in seeking His good pleasure and what He loves. This entails the heart turning towards God and directing itself to Him, the servant's striving being beneficial, earnest and not frivolous, and being sincere for the Face of God, not for show or reputation. This is the true religion, the one that is rightly called "religion" (dīn). As for one who claims to be upon the truth, claiming to be a possessor of religion and piety, yet has taken his religion as play and amusement, such that his heart is distracted from love of God and knowledge of Him, and he turns towards everything that harms him, and is diverted by his falsehood, and plays with his body in it, because work and striving that are for other than God are mere play. God has commanded that such a person be abandoned, be guarded against, not be deceived by him, that his condition be observed, that one beware of his deeds, and not be deceived by his obstruction from what brings one closer to God.

{And warn thereby} — i.e., warn by means of the Qur'an, explaining what benefits the servants in commands, and making it attractive by mentioning the attributes of goodness that it contains; and what harms the servants in prohibitions, explaining its kinds and clarifying the ugly and repugnant attributes it contains that call one to abandon it. All of this is so that {a soul may not be given over to ruin for what it has earned} — i.e., before the servant plunges into sins and dares against the Knower of the unseen and persists in that dreaded conduct. So warn it and admonish it, so that it may be restrained, deterred and refrain from doing it.

His saying: {It shall have, besides God, no protector and no intercessor} — i.e., before its sins encompass it, and then no one among the creation benefits it, neither relative nor friend; no one besides God takes it as a protector, and no intercessor intercedes for it. {And if it should offer every ransom} — i.e., it ransoms itself with every compensation, even if it were the filling of the earth with gold — {it will not be accepted from it} — i.e., it will not be accepted and will not avail. {Those} — the ones described by what was mentioned — {are those who have been given over to ruin} — i.e., they have been destroyed and despaired of good. That is {for what they earned. For them will be a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for what they used to disbelieve.} — i.e., water of extreme heat, whose heat has reached its limit, which scorches their faces and cuts through their intestines.

**Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 6, Verses 71–73**

{71} ﴿Say﴾: O Messenger, to the polytheists who associate others with God and call upon other than Him, who invite you to their religion, explaining and clarifying the description of their deities. A sensible person needs only the mention of their description to be turned away from them, for every sensible person who conceives the doctrine of the polytheists is certain of its falsehood before any proofs are established against it. This is a state that no person of sound judgment would accept. Its possessor is like ﴿the one whom the devils have lured in the earth﴾, that is, one whom they have led astray and bewildered, away from his path and method that lead to his destination, so that he remains ﴿bewildered, having companions who call him to guidance﴾, while the devils call him to ruin. He remains between the two callers, perplexed. This is the state of all people, except those whom God the Exalted has protected, for they find within themselves attractions and conflicting calls: the call of the Message, sound reason and upright nature call them to guidance and ascent to the highest heights, while the calls of Satan, of whoever follows his course, and of the commanding soul call them to misguidance and descent to the lowest depths. Indeed, this is the greatest blessing that God has bestowed upon the servants and the most complete upbringing that He has brought to them.

{74} Allah the Exalted says: Recount the story of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, praising him and magnifying him in the state of his calling to monotheism (tawhid) and his forbidding of association with others in worship (shirk). ﴿When Ibrahim said to his father Azar, "Do you take idols as gods? {75} ﴿And thus﴾: when We granted him success in monotheism and in calling to it, ﴿We showed Ibrahim the dominion (malakut) of the heavens and the earth﴾; that is, so that he might see with his insight what they contain of decisive proofs and shining evidences, ﴿and that he might be among the certain﴾: for in accordance with the establishment of the proofs, certainty and complete knowledge of all the matters are attained by him.

{76} ﴿So when the night covered him﴾; that is, it grew dark, ﴿he saw a star﴾: perhaps it was one of the bright stars, for singling it out for mention indicates that it exceeded others; and for this reason, Allah knows best, those who said it was Venus said so. ﴿He said, "This is my lord."﴾ That is, by way of condescension with the opponent; i.e., "This is my lord? **Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 6, verses 84–90:**

{84} ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob﴾: his son who is Israel, the father of the people (sha'b) whom God preferred over the worlds. ﴿Each of them﴾ We guided to the straight path, in their knowledge and their action. And ﴿Noah﴾ We guided ﴿before﴾, and his guidance is among the highest kinds of special guidance, which was not attained except by individuals from among mankind, namely the possessors of resolve (ulu al-'azm) among the messengers, of whom he is one. ﴿And from his offspring﴾: it is possible that the pronoun refers to Noah, since he is the nearest mentioned, and because God mentioned with those He mentioned Lot, who is from the offspring of Noah and not from the offspring of Abraham, as he was Abraham's nephew. It is also possible that the pronoun refers to Abraham, since the context is praise of him and commendation of him. Lot, although he was not of his offspring, was among those who believed at his hand, so the merit and excellence of the Friend (al-Khalil) in this is more eloquent than if he were merely a son of his. ﴿David and Solomon﴾, the son of David, ﴿and Job and Joseph﴾, the son of Jacob, ﴿and Moses and Aaron﴾, the two sons of 'Imran. ﴿And thus﴾: just as We set right the offspring of Abraham the Friend, because he excelled in the worship of his Lord and excelled in benefiting creation, so too ﴿We reward the good-doers﴾: by granting them true praise and righteous offspring in proportion to their good deeds.

{85} ﴿And Zachariah and John﴾: his son, ﴿and Jesus﴾, the son of Mary, ﴿and Elias—each﴾: of these ﴿is among the righteous﴾: in their character, their deeds and their knowledge. Indeed, they are the masters of the righteous, their leaders and their imams.

{86} ﴿And Ishmael﴾, the son of Abraham, the father of the people who are the best of peoples, namely the Arab people, and the father of the master of the children of Adam, Muhammad (ﷺ); ﴿and Jonah﴾, the son of Matthew; ﴿and Lot﴾, the son of Haran, brother of Abraham; ﴿each﴾ of these prophets and messengers ﴿We preferred over the worlds﴾: because the degrees of virtue are four, which God mentioned in His words: ﴿And whoever obeys God and the Messenger, those are with the ones whom God has blessed: the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous﴾. These are of the highest degree, and indeed they are the most excellent of the messengers absolutely. The messengers whom God related in His Book are without doubt more excellent than those whose stories He did not relate to us.

{87} ﴿And of their forefathers﴾; i.e., the fathers of those mentioned, ﴿and their offspring and their brothers﴾; i.e., and We guided some of the fathers of these, their offspring and their brothers. ﴿And We chose them﴾; i.e., We selected them, ﴿and We guided them to a straight path﴾.

{88–89} ﴿That﴾: the aforementioned guidance ﴿is the guidance of God﴾: there is no guidance except His guidance. ﴿He guides by it whom He wills of His servants﴾: so seek guidance from Him, for if He does not guide you, there is no guide for you besides Him. Among those whom He willed to guide were those mentioned. ﴿And if they had associated [others with God]﴾, by way of supposition and assumption, ﴿all that they used to do would have been nullified﴾: for shirk nullifies deeds and necessitates eternal abiding in the Fire. {90} ﴿Those﴾: the aforementioned ﴿are those whom God guided, so follow their guidance﴾; i.e., proceed, O Messenger, noble one, behind these good prophets, and follow their religion. The Prophet (ﷺ) complied and was guided by the guidance of the messengers before him, and he combined in himself every perfection found in them, so that he gathered virtues and distinctions by which he surpassed all the worlds. He was the master of the messengers and the imam of the God-fearing, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him and upon them all. It is by this consideration that some of the Companions who held this view deduced that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is the most excellent of all the messengers. ﴿Say﴾ to those who turned away from your call: ﴿"I do not ask you any wage for it"﴾; i.e., I do not seek from you any burden or wealth in return for my conveying to you and my calling you, lest it become one of the reasons for your refusal. ﴿My wage is only from God﴾. ﴿It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds﴾: by which they remember what benefits them so that they do it, and what harms them so that they abandon it, and by which they remember knowledge of their Lord through His names and attributes, and remember the praiseworthy character and the paths that lead to it, and the blameworthy character and the paths that lead to it. This is a denunciation of those among the Jews and the polytheists who deny prophethood and claim that God has sent down nothing upon any human being. Whoever says this has not measured God with His true measure, nor magnified Him with His true magnificence, for this is a disparagement of His wisdom, a claim that He leaves His servants neglected, not commanding them nor forbidding them, and a denial of the greatest favour God has bestowed upon His servants, namely prophethood, without which there is no path for the servants to attain happiness, honour and success. What greater disparagement of God is there than this?

﴿Say﴾ to them, binding them to the corruption of their statement and making them acknowledge what they themselves admit: ﴿Who sent down the Book which Moses brought﴾, namely the great Torah, ﴿as a light﴾ in the darknesses of ignorance, ﴿and a guidance﴾ from misguidance, and a guide to the straight path in knowledge and action. It is the Book which spread and became famous, whose mention filled hearts and ears, to the extent that they began to copy it onto parchments and to manipulate it as they wished: what agreed with their desires they revealed and made apparent, and what contradicted that they concealed and hid, and that is much. ﴿And you were taught﴾ of the knowledge that came through that glorious Book ﴿what neither you nor your fathers knew﴾.

So when you ask them who sent down this Book described with these attributes, answer this question and say ﴿Allah﴾, who sent it down; then the truth becomes clear and shines like the sun, and the proof is established against them. ﴿Then﴾, when you have thus bound them, ﴿leave them in their vain talk, playing﴾; that is, leave them to plunge into falsehood and to amuse themselves with what has no benefit, until they meet their Day which they are promised.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verse 92:

{92} That is: {And this}: the Qur'an which We have sent down {is a blessed Book}; that is, its description is blessing, due to the abundance of its goodness and the vastness of its benefits. {Confirming what was before it}; that is, it agrees with the previous Books and bears witness to their truth. {That you may warn the Mother of Cities and those around it}; that is, We have also sent it down so that you may warn the Mother of Cities, which is Makkah al-Mukarramah, and those around it from the lands of the Arabs, and indeed all the other towns, so that you warn people of the punishment of Allah and His seizing of nations, and warn them against whatever brings that about. {And those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it}: because when fear is in the heart, its pillars are firmly established and it submits to the pleasure of Allah. {And they are over their prayer, guarding it}; that is, they persist in it and preserve its pillars, its limits, its conditions, its etiquettes and its complements. May Allah make us among them.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verse 93–94:

{93} He, exalted is He, says: There is no one more unjust nor more wicked than one who lies against Allah by attributing to Allah a saying or a judgment, when He is free of it. This is the greatest injustice of all creation, because it includes lying and altering the religions, both their foundations and their branches, and attributing that to Allah, which is among the greatest corruptions. It includes the claim of prophethood, that Allah reveals to him, while he is lying in that. For he, along with his lying against Allah and his audacity toward His majesty and authority, obliges the creatures to follow him, fights them over that, and makes lawful the blood and property of whoever opposes him. This verse includes everyone who claimed prophethood, such as Musaylimah the Liar, al-Aswad al-Ansi, al-Mukhtar, and others who were characterized by this description. {And who says: "I will send down the like of what Allah has sent down."} That is: and who is more unjust than one who claims that he is able to do what Allah is able to do, and who competes with Allah in His rulings and legislates laws as Allah legislates. This includes everyone who claims that he is able to oppose the Qur'an and that it is within his power to bring its like! And what injustice is greater than the claim of the poor, weak, deficient in essence and deficient in every respect, to share with the strong, rich, who possesses absolute perfection in every respect in His essence, names and attributes?!

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verses 95–98:

{95} He, may He be exalted, informs of His perfection, the greatness of His dominion, the strength of His power, the vastness of His mercy, the generality of His generosity, and the intensity of His care for His creation, so He says: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Cleaver of the grain and the seed﴾. This encompasses all grains that people sow and those they do not sow, such as the grains that Allah scatters in the open lands and deserts. He cleaves the grains to produce crops and sprouts of all their varieties, shapes and benefits, and He cleaves the date-pit and other seeds to produce trees of date palms, fruits and other things. Thus creatures, human beings, livestock and beasts benefit, graze on what Allah has split from the grain and the seed, feed on it, and derive all kinds of benefits that Allah has placed in it. Allah shows them of His goodness and kindness that dazzles the intellects and bewilders the mighty, and He shows them of the wonders of His craftsmanship and the perfection of His wisdom, by which they recognize Him, affirm His oneness, and know that He is the Truth and that the worship of anything other than Him is false. ﴿He brings forth the living from the dead﴾: as He brings forth an animal from semen, a chick from an egg, and grain and trees from the seed and the pit. ﴿And brings forth the dead from the living﴾: that is, that which has no growth or no spirit, ﴿from the living﴾, as He brings forth seeds and grains from trees and crops, and brings forth eggs from birds and the like. ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾: the One who did what He did and alone created these things and arranged them; that is, the One who has divinity and worship over all His creatures, and who nurtures all the worlds with His blessings and feeds them with His generosity. ﴿So how are you turned away?﴾; that is, how are you diverted and turned away from worshipping the One of this description to worshipping one who possesses for himself no benefit, no harm, no death, no life, and no resurrection?

{96} When He, may He be exalted, mentioned the source of the creation of sustenance, He mentioned His favour in preparing dwellings and creating everything that the servants need of light and darkness, and what follows from that of various benefits and interests. So He says: ﴿Cleaver of the daybreak﴾; that is, just as He is the Cleaver of the grain and the seed, so He is the Cleaver of the darkness of the dark night, which covers what is on the face of the earth, with the light of dawn, which He splits gradually, until all the darkness of the night disappears and is succeeded by light and general brightness, by which creatures manage their interests, livelihoods, and the benefits of their religion and their worldly life.
Since creatures need tranquility, settledness, and rest, which cannot be completed without the presence of day and light, ﴿He has made﴾ the night a time of repose, in which human beings settle in their homes and for sleep, livestock settle in their shelters, and birds settle in their nests, so they take their share of rest; then Allah removes that with light, and so on forever until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And He made﴾ the sun and the moon as a means of reckoning, by which times and seasons are known, so the times of worship and the terms of transactions are regulated, and by which the duration of the past times is known. Were it not for the existence of the sun and the moon and their alternation and succession, the common people would not know that and would not share in its knowledge; rather, only individuals would know it after exertion, and essential interests would be lost accordingly. ﴿That is﴾ the aforementioned determination, ﴿the determination of the Mighty, the Knowing﴾: whose might has caused these great creations to submit to Him, so they run subjugated and made subservient by His command, such that they do not exceed what Allah has set for them, nor precede it, nor fall behind it; the Knowing whose knowledge encompasses the apparent and the hidden, the first and the last. Among the rational proofs of the comprehensiveness of His knowledge is the subjection of these great creations to a determination and a wondrous order, whose goodness, perfection, and conformity to interests and wisdoms bewilder the intellects.

{97} ﴿And He it is who placed for you the stars that you may be guided by them in the darknesses of the land and the sea﴾: when paths become confusing to you and the traveller is bewildered in his journey. Allah made the stars a guidance for creatures to the ways they need to take for their interests, trade, and travels. Among them are stars that are always seen and do not move from their place, and among them are those that are constantly in motion, whose movement is known to people of knowledge, by which they know the directions and times. This verse and the like indicate the legitimacy of learning the movements of the planets and their positions, which is called the science of navigation (ʿilm al-tasyīr), for guidance cannot be completed or achieved without it. ﴿We have detailed the signs﴾; that is, We have explained them, clarified them, and distinguished each kind and type from the other, such that Allah's signs have become manifest and apparent, ﴿for a people who know﴾; that is, for the people of knowledge and understanding, for they are the ones to whom the address is directed and from whom an answer is sought; unlike the people of ignorance and coarseness who turn away from Allah's signs and from the knowledge that the messengers brought, for clarification does not benefit them at all, detailing does not remove their confusion, and elucidation does not reveal to them any difficulty.

{98} ﴿And He it is who produced you from a single soul﴾: and that is Adam, peace be upon him. Allah produced from him this human element that has filled the earth and has never ceased to increase and grow, which varies in its characters, constitutions and attributes with a variation that cannot be controlled and whose description cannot be grasped. Allah has made for them a stays-place, that is, an end to which they come and a goal to which they are driven, and it is the abode of settlement, beyond which there is no abiding place and above which there is no end. This abode is that for which creatures were created to dwell, and they were brought into existence in this world to strive for its causes by which they are raised and through which it is built. As for this abode, it is a place of deposit and passage. ﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who understand﴾: about Allah's signs, and who understand from Him His proofs and clear evidences.
