Among the rational proofs of the comprehensiveness of His knowledge is the subjection of these great creations to a determination and a wondrous order, whose goodness, perfection, and conformity to interests and wisdoms bewilder the intellects.

{97} ﴿And He it is who placed for you the stars that you may be guided by them in the darknesses of the land and the sea﴾: when paths become confusing to you and the traveller is bewildered in his journey. Allah made the stars a guidance for creatures to the ways they need to take for their interests, trade, and travels. Among them are stars that are always seen and do not move from their place, and among them are those that are constantly in motion, whose movement is known to people of knowledge, by which they know the directions and times. This verse and the like indicate the legitimacy of learning the movements of the planets and their positions, which is called the science of navigation (ʿilm al-tasyīr), for guidance cannot be completed or achieved without it. ﴿We have detailed the signs﴾; that is, We have explained them, clarified them, and distinguished each kind and type from the other, such that Allah's signs have become manifest and apparent, ﴿for a people who know﴾; that is, for the people of knowledge and understanding, for they are the ones to whom the address is directed and from whom an answer is sought; unlike the people of ignorance and coarseness who turn away from Allah's signs and from the knowledge that the messengers brought, for clarification does not benefit them at all, detailing does not remove their confusion, and elucidation does not reveal to them any difficulty.

{98} ﴿And He it is who produced you from a single soul﴾: and that is Adam, peace be upon him. Allah produced from him this human element that has filled the earth and has never ceased to increase and grow, which varies in its characters, constitutions and attributes with a variation that cannot be controlled and whose description cannot be grasped. Allah has made for them a stays-place, that is, an end to which they come and a goal to which they are driven, and it is the abode of settlement, beyond which there is no abiding place and above which there is no end. This abode is that for which creatures were created to dwell, and they were brought into existence in this world to strive for its causes by which they are raised and through which it is built. Allah placed them in the loins of their fathers and the wombs of their mothers, then in the world, then in the barzakh; all of this in the manner of a deposit that does not settle or remain fixed, but is transferred from one to another, until they arrive at the abode which is the permanent stay. As for this abode, it is a place of deposit and passage. ﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who understand﴾: about Allah's signs, and who understand from Him His proofs and clear evidences.

This is among His greatest blessings, which creatures, both human and others, depend upon: He sent down water from the sky in successive showers at the time people needed it, and by it God caused to grow everything that people and livestock eat. Creatures graze and spread out by the bounty of God, rejoice in His provision, and are glad in His kindness; dryness, despair and drought depart from them. Hearts rejoice, faces brighten, and the servants obtain from the mercy of the Most Merciful that by which they enjoy and graze, which obliges them to exert their utmost effort in thanking the One who bestowed the blessings, worshipping Him, turning to Him in repentance, and loving Him.

When He mentioned the general growth produced by water, of various kinds of trees and plants, He singled out grain and palm trees because of their great benefit and because they are the staple food of most people. So He said: ﴿Then We brought forth from it green [shoots], from which We bring forth grain piled up﴾; that is, from that green vegetation, ﴿grain piled up﴾: one layer upon another, of wheat, barley, millet, rice and other kinds of crops. Describing it as "piled up" indicates that its grains are many and varied, all drawing from one substance, yet they do not mix; rather they are separate grains with common roots. It also indicates their abundance and the wide scope of their yield and produce, so that enough seed remains for planting and a large remainder remains for eating and storing. ﴿And from the palm trees﴾: God brings forth ﴿from their spathes﴾, which is the sheath and the covering before the cluster appears from it, and from that covering ﴿come clusters hanging low﴾; that is, near, easy to reach, hanging down upon whoever wants them, such that reaching the fruit from the palm is not difficult even if the palm is tall, for in it there are footholds and steps that make climbing easy. ﴿And﴾: God brought forth by the water ﴿gardens of grapevines, and the olive and the pomegranate﴾. These are among the trees of great benefit and great importance, so God singled them out for mention after having generalized all trees and plants. His saying ﴿similar and dissimilar﴾ may refer to the pomegranate and the olive: that is, similar in their trees and leaves, but dissimilar in their fruit. It may also refer to all trees and fruits, meaning that some of them are similar, resembling one another and close in some of their attributes, while others have no resemblance between them and anything else; all of them benefit the servants, who enjoy them, eat them, and take lessons from them. For this reason God commanded reflection upon them, saying: ﴿Look﴾: a looking of reflection and contemplation ﴿at their fruit﴾; that is, at all trees, especially the palm, ﴿when it bears fruit and [at] its ripening﴾; that is, look at it at the time of its bearing and at the time of its ripening and maturity. Indeed, in that are lessons and signs by which one may infer God's mercy, the vastness of His kindness and generosity, His perfect power, and His care for His servants. But not everyone takes lessons or reflects, and not everyone who reflects grasps the intended meaning. For this reason God restricted benefiting from the signs to the believers, saying: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾, for the believers, by what they possess of faith, are moved to act upon its requirements and necessary consequences, among which is reflecting upon the signs of God and drawing from them what is intended and what they indicate by reason, natural disposition, and revelation.

{100} God, exalted is He, informs us that, despite His kindness to His servants and His making Himself known to them through His clear signs and manifest proofs, those who associated partners with Him, among the Quraysh and others, took for Him partners whom they invoke and worship, from among the jinn and the angels. These are creatures of God's creation, and none of them has any of the distinctive attributes of lordship (rububiyyah) or divinity (uluhiyyah). Yet they made these partners equal to the One who holds creation and command, who bestows every kind of blessing and repels every calamity. Likewise, the polytheists ﴿invented falsehoods﴾, that is, they fabricated and forged, of their own accord, ﴿sons and daughters for God, without knowledge﴾. ﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates against God without knowledge﴾, and attributes to Him the most shameful deficiency, from which God must be declared free? For this reason He declared Himself free of what the polytheists attributed to Him, saying: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted above what they describe﴾. Indeed, He is described by every perfection and is free of every deficiency, defect and flaw.

{101} ﴿The Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, their Creator, who perfected their making without any prior model, with the best creation, order and splendor, such that the minds of people of understanding could not conceive the like of it. He has no partner in their creation. ﴿How can He have a son when He has no consort?﴾ That is, how could God have a son, when He is the God, the Lord, the Eternal Refuge (al-Samad) who has no consort, that is, no wife? He is free of need of His creatures, while all of them are needy of Him and in every state dependent upon Him. A son must be of the same kind as his father, but God is the Creator of everything, and none of the created beings resembles God in any respect. Having mentioned the generality of His creation of things, He then mentioned the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of them, saying: ﴿And He is Knowing of all things﴾. Mentioning knowledge after creation points to the rational proof of His knowledge, namely these created beings and the perfect order and wondrous creation they contain, for this indicates the vastness of the Creator's knowledge and the perfection of His wisdom. As He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Should not He who created know? And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾, and as He said: ﴿And He is the Creator, the Knowing﴾.

{102} ﴿That is God, your Lord﴾ who created what He created and decreed what He decreed. ﴿There is no god but Him﴾, that is, the One who is worshipped and taken as God, who deserves the utmost humility and the utmost love, the Lord who nurtures all creation with blessings and turns away from them every kind of calamity, the Creator of everything. ﴿So worship Him﴾: that is, once it is established and affirmed that He is God, there is no god but Him, then direct all kinds of worship to Him alone, make them sincerely for God, and seek thereby His countenance, for this is the purpose of creation for which they were created: ﴿I did not create the jinn and humankind except to worship Me﴾. ﴿And He is Guardian over all things﴾, that is, all things are under God's trusteeship (wakalah), management and direction, in creation, governance and disposal. It is well known that the affairs being administered are sound, complete and perfectly ordered according to the condition of the one in charge of them. God's trusteeship over things is not of the same kind as the trusteeship of creatures, for their trusteeship is a deputyship (niyabah), and the deputy is subordinate to the one who appointed him. As for the Creator, blessed and exalted is He, His trusteeship derives from Himself for Himself, and includes perfect knowledge, excellent management, goodness in it and justice. No one can therefore find fault with God, nor see in His creation any flaw or defect, nor any shortcoming or imperfection in His governance. Among His trusteeship is that He, exalted is He, undertook to explain His religion and preserve it from whatever would remove or alter it, and that He took charge of protecting the believers and keeping them from whatever would remove their faith and religion.

{103} ﴿Vision does not encompass Him﴾, due to His greatness, majesty and perfection. That is, eyes do not comprehend Him, although they see Him and rejoice in gazing upon His noble countenance. Negating comprehension (idrak) does not negate sight (ru'yah); rather, it affirms it by implication, for when He negates comprehension, which is the most specific attribute of sight, this shows that sight is established. Had He intended to negate sight, He would have said: ﴿Vision does not see Him﴾ or something similar. Thus it is known that the verse contains no proof for the doctrine of the Mu'attilah (those who deny the attributes), who deny the vision of their Lord in the Hereafter. Rather, it contains what indicates the opposite of their position. ﴿And He comprehends vision﴾, that is, He is the One whose knowledge encompasses the outward and the inward, whose hearing encompasses all sounds, whether apparent or hidden, and whose sight encompasses all things seen, small and great. For this reason He said: ﴿And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾, that is, the One whose knowledge and awareness are so subtle and fine that He perceives secrets, hidden things, concealed matters and innermost thoughts. Among His subtlety is that He leads His servant to the interests of his religion, and brings them to him by means the servant does not perceive and does not strive for, and brings him to eternal happiness and everlasting success from where he does not expect. He even decrees for him things he dislikes and suffers from and asks God to remove, because He knows that his religion is better served by them and that his perfection depends upon them. Glory be to the Subtle who does what He wills, the Merciful to the believers.

{104} ﴿There have come to you clear evidences from your Lord. So whoever sees, it is for his own soul, and whoever is blind, it is against it. And I am not a guardian over you﴾. Having explained the clear signs and manifest proofs indicating the truth in all matters and aims, God, exalted is He, alerted the servants to them and informed them that their guidance and its opposite are for their own souls. He said: ﴿There have come to you clear evidences from your Lord﴾, that is, signs that make the truth clear and place it in the heart as the sun is placed before the eyes, because of their eloquence, clarity, explicitness, and their conformity with sublime meanings and beautiful realities, for they proceed from the Lord who nurtured His creation with blessings both outward and inward, the greatest and most excellent of which is the clarification of signs and the explanation of difficulties. ﴿Whoever sees﴾ through those signs the places of lesson and acts according to their requirement, ﴿it is for his own soul﴾, for God is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy. Whoever is blind, in that he is given sight but does not see clearly, is admonished but does not heed, and the truth is made clear to him but he neither submits to it nor humbles himself, his blindness only harms himself. ﴿And I am not﴾, O Messenger, ﴿a guardian over you﴾, one who guards your deeds and constantly watches them. My duty is only the clear conveyance, and I have discharged it and conveyed what was sent down to me. This is my function, and beyond it I am not appointed.

{102} ﴿That is God, your Lord﴾ who created what He created and decreed what He decreed. ﴿There is no god but Him﴾, that is, the One who is worshipped and taken as God, who deserves the utmost humility and the utmost love, the Lord who nurtures all creation with blessings and turns away from them every kind of calamity, the Creator of everything. ﴿So worship Him﴾: that is, once it is established and affirmed that He is God, there is no god but Him, then direct all kinds of worship to Him alone, make them sincerely for God, and seek thereby His countenance, for this is the purpose of creation for which they were created: ﴿I did not create the jinn and humankind except to worship Me﴾. ﴿And He is Guardian over all things﴾, that is, all things are under God's trusteeship (wakalah), management and direction, in creation, governance and disposal. It is well known that the affairs being administered are sound, complete and perfectly ordered according to the condition of the one in charge of them. God's trusteeship over things is not of the same kind as the trusteeship of creatures, for their trusteeship is a deputyship (niyabah), and the deputy is subordinate to the one who appointed him. As for the Creator, blessed and exalted is He, His trusteeship derives from Himself for Himself, and includes perfect knowledge, excellent management, goodness in it and justice. No one can therefore find fault with God, nor see in His creation any flaw or defect, nor any shortcoming or imperfection in His governance. Among His trusteeship is that He, exalted is He, undertook to explain His religion and preserve it from whatever would remove or alter it, and that He took charge of protecting the believers and keeping them from whatever would remove their faith and religion.

{103} ﴿Vision does not encompass Him﴾, due to His greatness, majesty and perfection. That is, eyes do not comprehend Him, although they see Him and rejoice in gazing upon His noble countenance. Negating comprehension (idrak) does not negate sight (ru'yah); rather, it affirms it by implication, for when He negates comprehension, which is the most specific attribute of sight, this shows that sight is established. Had He intended to negate sight, He would have said: ﴿Vision does not see Him﴾ or something similar. Thus it is known that the verse contains no proof for the doctrine of the Mu'attilah (those who deny the attributes), who deny the vision of their Lord in the Hereafter. Rather, it contains what indicates the opposite of their position. ﴿And He comprehends vision﴾, that is, He is the One whose knowledge encompasses the outward and the inward, whose hearing encompasses all sounds, whether apparent or hidden, and whose sight encompasses all things seen, small and great. For this reason He said: ﴿And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾, that is, the One whose knowledge and awareness are so subtle and fine that He perceives secrets, hidden things, concealed matters and innermost thoughts. Among His subtlety is that He leads His servant to the interests of his religion, and brings them to him by means the servant does not perceive and does not strive for, and brings him to eternal happiness and everlasting success from where he does not expect. He even decrees for him things he dislikes and suffers from and asks God to remove, because He knows that his religion is better served by them and that his perfection depends upon them. Glory be to the Subtle who does what He wills, the Merciful to the believers.

{104} ﴿There have come to you clear evidences from your Lord. So whoever sees, it is for his own soul, and whoever is blind, it is against it. And I am not a guardian over you﴾. Having explained the clear signs and manifest proofs indicating the truth in all matters and aims, God, exalted is He, alerted the servants to them and informed them that their guidance and its opposite are for their own souls. He said: ﴿There have come to you clear evidences from your Lord﴾, that is, signs that make the truth clear and place it in the heart as the sun is placed before the eyes, because of their eloquence, clarity, explicitness, and their conformity with sublime meanings and beautiful realities, for they proceed from the Lord who nurtured His creation with blessings both outward and inward, the greatest and most excellent of which is the clarification of signs and the explanation of difficulties. ﴿Whoever sees﴾ through those signs the places of lesson and acts according to their requirement, ﴿it is for his own soul﴾, for God is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy. Whoever is blind, in that he is given sight but does not see clearly, is admonished but does not heed, and the truth is made clear to him but he neither submits to it nor humbles himself, his blindness only harms himself. ﴿And I am not﴾, O Messenger, ﴿a guardian over you﴾, one who guards your deeds and constantly watches them. My duty is only the clear conveyance, and I have discharged it and conveyed what was sent down to me. This is my function, and beyond it I am not appointed.

{100} God, exalted is He, informs us that, despite His kindness to His servants and His making Himself known to them through His clear signs and manifest proofs, those who associated partners with Him, among the Quraysh and others, took for Him partners whom they invoke and worship, from among the jinn and the angels. These are creatures of God's creation, and none of them has any of the distinctive attributes of lordship (rububiyyah) or divinity (uluhiyyah). Yet they made these partners equal to the One who holds creation and command, who bestows every kind of blessing and repels every calamity. Likewise, the polytheists ﴿invented falsehoods﴾, that is, they fabricated and forged, of their own accord, ﴿sons and daughters for God, without knowledge﴾. ﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates against God without knowledge﴾, and attributes to Him the most shameful deficiency, from which God must be declared free? For this reason He declared Himself free of what the polytheists attributed to Him, saying: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted above what they describe﴾. Indeed, He is described by every perfection and is free of every deficiency, defect and flaw.

{101} ﴿The Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, their Creator, who perfected their making without any prior model, with the best creation, order and splendor, such that the minds of people of understanding could not conceive the like of it. He is free of need of His creatures, while all of them are needy of Him and in every state dependent upon Him. A son must be of the same kind as his father, but God is the Creator of everything, and none of the created beings resembles God in any respect. {108} God forbids the believers from an action that was in principle permissible, indeed lawful, namely reviling the gods of the polytheists, those that they have taken as idols and deities alongside God, and through whose abuse and denigration one might draw near to God. But since this reviling would become a means to the polytheists reviling the Lord of the worlds, who must be exalted above every defect, blemish, insult and slander, God forbade reviling the gods of the polytheists. For they are zealous for their religion and fanatical about it, since every community has had its deeds made attractive to it by God, so they see them as good, defend them, and protect them by every means. Indeed, they would revile God, the Lord of the worlds, whose greatness is firmly established in the hearts of the righteous and the wicked, if the Muslims reviled their gods. Yet all creatures will return to God on the Day of Resurrection and their final end is with Him: they will be presented before Him and their deeds will be presented, and He will inform them of what they used to do, of good and of evil.

In this noble verse is evidence for the legal principle that means are judged by the ends to which they lead, and that the means to something forbidden, even if permissible in itself, become forbidden when they lead to evil.

{109} That is: the polytheists who denied the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) swore by God "with the utmost of their oaths", meaning they swore an oath in which they exerted themselves and made it emphatic: "If a sign comes to them" that indicates the truthfulness of Muhammad (ﷺ), "they will surely believe in it." This statement that came from them was not intended for guidance; rather, their aim was to repel the objection against them and to reject what the Messenger brought, definitively. For God supported His Messenger (ﷺ) with clear signs and manifest proofs which, upon reflection, leave no slightest doubt or difficulty regarding the truth of what he brought. Therefore their demand for signs after that is from the category of obstinacy, which does not necessitate a response. Indeed, refraining from answering them may even be better for them, for God's custom with His servants is that those who demand signs from their messengers, when the signs come to them and they do not believe in them, He hastens to punish them. For this reason He said: "Say: The signs are only with God", that is, it is He who sends them when He wills and withholds them when He wills; "I have no part in the affair." So your demand of me for signs is an injustice and a demand for what I do not possess. You are only directed to clarifying what I have brought you and confirming it, and that has occurred. Nevertheless, it is not known that if signs came to them they would believe and affirm; rather, the general case of one in this state is that he does not believe. For this reason He said: "And what will make you aware that when they come, they will not believe?"

{110} "And We turn their hearts and their eyes away, just as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly." That is: We will punish them if they do not believe the first time the caller comes to them and the proof is established against them, by turning hearts around, placing a barrier between them and faith, and withholding success in following the straight path. This is from God's justice and wisdom toward His servants, for they are the ones who brought harm upon themselves: the door was opened for them but they did not enter, and the way was shown to them but they did not take it. So after that, when they are deprived of success, it is fitting to their condition.

{111} Likewise, their conditioning of faith upon their own will and desire alone, and their not relying upon God, is among the greatest errors. For even if the great signs came to them, such as the descent of angels to them bearing witness to the Messenger's prophethood, the speaking of the dead and their resurrection after death, and We gathered upon them every thing, so that it would speak to them face to face, directly, confirming the truth of what the Messenger brought, faith would not have come about for them unless God willed their faith. But most of them are ignorant. Therefore they made their faith depend merely upon the coming of signs. Rather, true intellect and knowledge consist in the servant having as his aim the pursuit of the truth, seeking it by the means God has explained, acting upon that, seeking his Lord's help in following it, not relying on himself, his own power or strength, and not demanding from signs of proposal anything that has no benefit in it.

{112} The Exalted says, consoling His Messenger [Muhammad] (ﷺ): Just as We have made for you enemies who reject your call and fight against you and envy you, so too is this Our way: We make for every prophet whom We send to the creation enemies from the devils of mankind and the jinn, who act in opposition to what the messengers brought. {Some of them inspire to others ornamented speech as deception.} That is: some of them embellish for others the matter to which they call, which is falsehood, and they adorn its expressions so as to present it in its finest form, so that the foolish are deceived by it and the ignorant, who do not understand realities nor comprehend meanings, are led along by it. Rather, ornamented words and deceptive phrases impress them, so they take truth to be falsehood and falsehood to be truth.

{113} For this reason the Exalted said: {And that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it}; that is: so that they may incline toward that ornamented speech. {The hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter} incline to it, because their lack of belief in the Last Day and the absence of beneficial intellects drive them to it. {And that they may be pleased with it}: after they have listened to it. They listen to it first, and when they incline to it and see those pleasing expressions, they become pleased with it; it becomes adorned in their hearts and turns into a firm belief and a constant characteristic. From this there follows that they commit {what they are committing}; that is: they bring forth, by word and deed, lies that are among the necessary consequences of those corrupt beliefs. This is the condition of the deceivers, the devils of mankind and the jinn, who respond to their call.

As for the people of faith in the Hereafter and those of sound intellect and weighty minds, they are not deceived by those expressions, nor are they seduced by those embellishments. Rather, their resolve is directed toward knowing realities; they look at the meanings to which the callers summon. If they are true, they accept them and submit to them, even if they are clothed in ugly expressions and inadequate words. And if they are false, they reject them from the one who said them, whoever he may be, even if he dresses them in the most pleasing expressions, finer than silk.

Among the wisdom of Allah the Exalted in making enemies for the prophets, and in making supporters for falsehood who stand up to call to it, is that His servants may be tested and examined, so that the truthful may be distinguished from the liar, the intelligent from the ignorant, and the seeing from the blind. And among His wisdom: in that there is a clarification of the truth and an explanation of it, for truth shines forth and becomes clear when falsehood stands up to contend with and oppose it; then there becomes evident, from the proofs and evidences of the truth which indicate its veracity and reality, and from the corruption and nullity of falsehood, what is among the greatest of the aims over which competitors compete.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verse 114–115:

{114} That is: Say, O Messenger: ﴿Shall I seek a judge other than Allah?﴾ I would take Him as judge, and bind myself to His commands and prohibitions. For other than Allah is one who is judged, not a judge, and every governance and judgment of a created being contains imperfection, defect, and injustice. What must be taken as judge is Allah alone, without partner, to whom belong the creation and the command. ﴿He it is who has sent down to you the Book, fully detailed﴾; that is, clarifying within it the lawful and the unlawful, the legal rulings, and the foundations of the religion and its branches. There is no clarification above His clarification, no proof more manifest than His proof, no judgment better than His judgment, and no word more upright, for His rulings contain wisdom and mercy. The People of the earlier Scriptures, Jews and Christians, acknowledge this, and ﴿they know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth﴾. For this reason the reports agree, so ﴿do not be among the doubters﴾ concerning this, nor ﴿be among the disputers﴾.

{115} Then He described its detail, saying: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾; that is, truthful in its reports and just in its commands and prohibitions. There is nothing more truthful than the reports of Allah which He has deposited in this Mighty Book, and nothing more just than His commands and prohibitions. ﴿None can alter His words﴾, for He has preserved them and perfected them with the highest kinds of truthfulness and the utmost reality, so it is impossible to change them or to propose anything better than them. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾ of all voices, despite the variety of languages and the diversity of needs, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾, whose knowledge encompasses the outward and the inward, the past and the future.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verses 116–117:

{116} Allah says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), warning him against obeying the majority of people: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah﴾. For most of them have deviated in their religion, their deeds and their knowledge. Their religion is corrupt, their deeds follow their desires, and their knowledge contains no verification and does not lead to the right path. Rather, their end is that they follow mere conjecture, which avails nothing against the truth, and they fabricate lies against Allah about what they do not know.

{117} Whoever is in this condition is deserving that Allah warn His servants against him and describe his states to them. For although this is an address to the Prophet (ﷺ), his community is a model for him in all the rulings that are not specific to him. Allah is the most truthful in speech and the most truthful in statement, and ﴿He knows best who strays from His way﴾, and who is guided and guides others. So it is obligatory upon you, O believers, to follow His advice, commands and prohibitions, for He knows best what is in your interest and is more merciful to you than you are to yourselves.

This verse indicates that the truth is not established by the large number of its adherents, and that the fewness of those who follow a matter does not mean it is not true. Rather, the reality is the opposite: the people of truth are the fewest in number but the greatest in standing and reward with Allah. Rather, it is obligatory to establish the truth and falsehood by the means that lead to them.

**Verses 118–119:** God commands His believing servants, in keeping with the requirements of faith, that if they are believers they should eat of what the name of God has been mentioned over, from the livestock cattle and other permitted animals. They should also affirm that these are lawful. They should not do as the people of the jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) did, forbidding many lawful things by innovation of their own making and by misguidance from their devils. God has stated that a mark of the believer is to oppose the people of the jahiliyyah in this blameworthy custom, which involves altering God's law. He also asks: what prevents them from eating what the name of God has been mentioned over? God has explained in detail to His servants what He has forbidden to them, clarified it and made it evident. Therefore no ambiguity or doubt remains that would justify refraining from some lawful food out of fear of falling into what is unlawful.

This noble verse shows that the basic ruling on things and foods is permissibility. If the Law has not stated the prohibition of something, it remains permissible. What God has left unmentioned is lawful, because God has detailed what is forbidden, so whatever He has not detailed is not forbidden. Nevertheless, what God has detailed and made clear as forbidden is permitted in cases of necessity and extreme hunger, as He said: ﴿Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine…﴾ until He said: ﴿But whoever is compelled by necessity, neither desiring it nor exceeding the limit, then indeed your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Then He warned against many of the people, saying: ﴿And indeed, many [of them] lead [others] astray by their desires without knowledge﴾; that is, merely by what their souls desire, ﴿without knowledge﴾, meaning without proof or evidence. So the servant should beware of such people. Their mark, as God has described them to His servants, is that their call is not founded on any clear proof, and they have no valid legal argument. They only have specious claims in accordance with their corrupt desires and deficient opinions. These people are transgressors against the Law of God and against the servants of God, and God does not love transgressors. This is in contrast to the guiding and rightly guided people, who call to truth and guidance and support their call with rational and textual proofs. In their call they follow nothing but the pleasure of their Lord and drawing near to Him.

{120} By "sin" (al-ithm) is meant all acts of disobedience that make a servant sinful, that is, that bring him into sin and hardship concerning matters connected to the rights of God and the rights of His servants. God has forbidden His servants from committing outward and inward sin, that is, what is open and what is hidden: that connected to the body and its limbs, and that connected to the heart. A servant cannot abandon outward and inward acts of disobedience except after knowing them and searching for them. Therefore, searching for them, knowing the disobediences of the heart and the body, and having knowledge of this is an obligation that is individually binding (wajib muta'ayyan) upon the mukallaf (the responsible adult). Many people are unaware of many disobediences, especially those of the heart, such as arrogance (al-kibr), self-admiration (al-'ujb), showing off (al-riya')... and the like, to the extent that many of them are committed by him while he neither senses nor perceives them. This is a result of turning away from knowledge and lacking insight.

Then God, exalted is He, informs that those who earn outward and inward sin will be recompensed according to their earnings and in proportion to their sins, whether few or many. This recompense will occur in the Hereafter, and it may also occur in this world: the servant is punished, and by that some of his evil deeds are lightened for him.

{121} What is forbidden here includes that over which the name of other than God has been pronounced, such as what is slaughtered for idols and the gods of the polytheists. This is indeed what has been made unlawful specifically by explicit text, "that over which the name of other than God has been invoked" (6:145).

Included in this also is that over which the name of God was not mentioned, of what is slaughtered for God, such as sacrificial animals and offerings, or for meat and eating, if the slaughterer deliberately leaves out the naming, according to many scholars. Excluded from this general ruling is the one who forgets, by the other texts that indicate the lifting of hardship from him.

Also included in this verse is what dies without proper slaughter (dhakah) among carrion, for it is among what the name of God has not been mentioned over. God specifically mentioned it in His saying, "Forbidden to you are carrion" (5:3). Perhaps it was the cause of the revelation of the verse, based on His saying, "Indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you" (6:121) without knowledge. When the polytheists heard God and His Messenger prohibit carrion and permit what is slaughtered, and they used to consider carrion lawful, they said in opposition to God and His Messenger and in dispute without proof or evidence: "Do you eat what you kill, but not what God kills?" meaning by that carrion! This is a corrupt opinion that is not based on proof or evidence, but rather on their corrupt opinions. Had the truth followed them, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been corrupted. So woe to those who place these minds above the law of God and His rulings, which accord with the general welfare and the private benefits. This is not surprising from them, for these opinions and their like proceed from the inspiration of their allies among the devils, who want to lead creation astray from their religion and call them to be among the companions of the blazing fire.

"And if you obey them" (6:121): in their polytheism and their making lawful what is unlawful and making unlawful what is lawful, "indeed you would be polytheists" (6:121), because you have taken them as allies besides God and agreed with them in what has separated them from the Muslims; therefore your path is their path.

This noble verse indicates that what falls into the hearts of inspirations and unveilings, which occur frequently among the Sufis and their like, does not by itself indicate that it is true, nor is it to be believed until it is presented to the Book of God and the Sunnah of His Messenger. If both testify to its acceptance, it is accepted; if it contradicts them, it is rejected; and if nothing of that is known, one withholds judgment on it, neither believing nor disbelieving it, because inspiration may come from the Merciful and may come from the Satan. Therefore there must be distinction between them and discernment. By failing to distinguish between the two matters, there has occurred of error and misguidance what none can count except God.

{122} God Most High says: {Is one who was dead} — before God guided him — {and We gave him life} — with the light of knowledge, faith and obedience — so that he walks among the people in light, seeing clearly in his affairs, guided on his path, knowing good and loving it, striving to enact it in himself and in others, knowing evil and hating it, striving to abandon it and remove it from himself and from others. Is this one equal to the one who is in darkness, the darkness of ignorance, error, unbelief and sins, {not coming out of it}? Paths have become confused for him and his routes have grown dark, so worry, distress, grief and misery overtake him. God Most High thus alerts minds, through what they perceive and recognise, that this one and that one are not equal, just as night and day, light and darkness, the living and the dead, are not equal. It is as if it were said: how could one with the least measure of intellect prefer to be in this state, and to remain in darkness, bewildered? He answers that {what they used to do was made attractive to the disbelievers}. Satan did not cease to beautify their deeds for them and adorn them in their hearts until they came to consider them good and to regard them as true, and this became a belief in their hearts and an established, enduring quality of theirs. For this reason they were content with the evil and vileness in which they were.

{123} Those who are in darkness, wandering blindly and hesitating in their falsehood, are not equal: among them are leaders, chiefs and those who are followed, and among them are followers and subordinates. The first of them are those who have attained the most wretched of states. For this reason He said: {And thus We placed in every town great ones of its criminals} — that is, the chiefs whose sin has grown great and whose tyranny has become intense — {to plot therein}: by deception, by calling to the path of Satan, and by opposing the messengers and their followers with word and deed. Yet their plotting and scheming only rebounds upon themselves, for they plot, and God plots, and God is the best of plotters.

Likewise, God makes the great imams of guidance and their most excellent ones contend against these criminals, refute their statements, strive against them in the way of God, and pursue the means that lead to that. God helps them, guides their judgment, makes their feet firm, and alternates the days between them and their enemies, until the affair turns in its outcome to their victory and dominance. And the good end belongs to the righteous.

{124} The great criminals only persisted in their falsehood and rejected the truth that the messengers brought out of envy and transgression. They said: {We will not believe until we are given what was given to the messengers of God}: prophethood and messengership. In this there is an objection against God, self-admiration, arrogance toward the truth He sent down through His messengers, and a narrowing of God's bounty and grace. God refuted their corrupt objection and informed that they are not fit for good, and that there is nothing in them that would warrant their being among the righteous servants of God, let alone among the prophets and messengers. So He said: {God knows best where to place His message}. Whoever He knows is fit for it, and will bear its burdens, and is characterised by every beautiful disposition and free of every base trait, God gives him what His wisdom requires, both primarily and secondarily. And whoever is not like that, He does not place His finest gifts with one who is not worthy of them and in whom they would not thrive.

In this verse is evidence of the perfection of God's wisdom, for although He is Most Merciful, of vast generosity and abundant kindness, He is also Wise, and does not place His bounty except with those who deserve it. Then He threatened the criminals, saying: {Humiliation from God will befall those who committed crime} — that is, disgrace and abasement, just as they were arrogant toward the truth, God humbled them — {and severe punishment because of what they used to plot}: because of their scheming, not as an injustice from Him, Most High.

Allah the Exalted says, explaining to His servants the sign of a servant's happiness and guidance, and the sign of his wretchedness and misguidance: Whoever has his chest expanded to Islam, that is, it becomes broad and spacious, is illuminated by the light of faith, and is revived by the radiance of certainty, so that his soul is reassured by it. He loves goodness, and his soul makes its performance easy for him, so that he enjoys it and does not find it burdensome. This is a sign that Allah has guided him, bestowed upon him success, and set him on the most upright path. The sign of the one whom Allah wills to misguide is that Allah makes his chest narrow and constricted, that is, in extreme constriction with respect to faith, knowledge, and certainty. His heart has been immersed in doubts and desires, so no good reaches it, and his heart does not expand to do good. It is as if, because of its narrowness and tightness, he is nearly ascending into the sky, that is, as if he were being charged with an impossible ascent into the sky, against which there is no remedy. The cause of this is their lack of faith. It is what made it necessary for Allah to place the defilement upon them, because they closed off for themselves the door of mercy and kindness. This is a balance that does not waver and a path that does not change: whoever gives and fears Allah, and affirms the best reward, Allah will make easy for him the path to ease; and whoever is miserly and considers himself self-sufficient, and denies the best reward, then We shall make easy for him the path to hardship.

{126} That is: moderate, leading to God and to the abode of His honour. Its rulings have been made clear, its laws detailed, and good distinguished from evil. But this detailing and clarification is not for everyone; rather it is "for a people who remember," for they are the ones who knew and benefited from their knowledge, and God has prepared for them a great reward and a beautiful recompense.

{127} Therefore He said: ﴿For them is the abode of peace with their Lord﴾. Paradise is called the Abode of Peace because it is safe from every defect, blight, turbidity, worry, grief, and other troubles. It follows from this that its bliss is at the utmost degree of perfection and the completion of its completeness, such that describers cannot describe it and those who wish cannot wish for anything beyond it, both the bliss of the spirit, the heart and the body. For them therein is what their souls desire and what delights the eyes, and they will abide therein. ﴿And He is their Walī (Protector/Ally)﴾: the One who took charge of their management and upbringing, was gentle with them in all their affairs, helped them to obey Him, and made easy for them every means that leads to His love. He took them as allies only because of their righteous deeds and the preliminaries by which they sought the pleasure of their Master, unlike one who turns away from his Master and follows his own desire; for him, Satan is empowered over him, so he takes him as an ally, and he corrupts for him his religion and his worldly life.

{128} He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And [mention] the Day He will gather them all together﴾; that is, all of the two weighty beings, mankind and jinn, those who went astray and those who led others astray. Then He will rebuke the jinn who misled mankind, adorned evil for them, and incited them to sins: ﴿O company of jinn, you have led astray a great many of mankind﴾; that is, you have misled them and turned them away from the way of God. How, then, did you dare to violate My sacred prohibitions, defy My messengers, stand as warriors against God, and strive to turn the servants of God away from His way toward the path of Hellfire? ﴿Today, My curse is due upon you, and My retribution is incumbent upon you, and We shall increase you in punishment in accordance with your disbelief and your misguidance of others.﴾ You will have no excuse by which you may apologize, no refuge to which you may flee, no intercessor who will intercede, and no supplication that will be heard. {129} ﴿And thus do We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn﴾; that is, just as We empowered the rebellious jinn and gave them authority to mislead their allies among mankind, and bound them together with the bond of friendship and agreement because of their own earning and striving in that, so too it is part of Our way that We make every wrongdoer an ally of a wrongdoer like himself, who incites him toward evil, urges him to it, makes him averse to good, and repels him from it. {130} Then God rebuked all those among the jinn and mankind who turned away from the truth and rejected it, and clarified their error, and they acknowledged it. {132} But although they share in the loss, they differ greatly in its measure. ﴿And for each are degrees according to what they did﴾; that is, according to their deeds. {133} God only commanded His servants to do righteous deeds and forbade them from evil deeds out of mercy toward them and intent for their welfare. {132} But although they share in the loss, they differ greatly in its measure. ﴿And for each are degrees according to what they did﴾; that is, according to their deeds. The one who committed little evil is not treated like the one who committed much, nor is the follower like the leader, nor the subordinate like the chief. Likewise, the people of reward and Paradise, although they share in profit, success, and entry into Paradise, there are among them differences that no one knows but God, and yet they all [have] been pleased with what their Master has given them and content with what He has bestowed. {133} God only commanded His servants to do righteous deeds and forbade them from evil deeds out of mercy toward them and intent for their welfare. {134} The heedless one who turns away should not consider the swift arrival of this abode unlikely, for ﴿what you are promised is coming, and you cannot escape﴾ God, fleeing from His punishment, for your forelocks are in His grip, and you are under His management and disposal.

{135} ﴿Say﴾: O Messenger, to your people, when you have summoned them to God, clarified to them their final end and what is due to Him from them, and they refused to submit to His command, followed their desires, and persisted in their polytheism: ﴿O my people, act according to your position﴾; that is, according to your state in which you are, which you have accepted for yourselves. ﴿Indeed, I am acting﴾ in accordance with God's command and following the pleasure of God. ﴿You will know to whom will belong the final outcome of the abode﴾: me or you. {134} The heedless one who turns away should not consider the swift arrival of this abode unlikely, for ﴿what you are promised is coming, and you cannot escape﴾ God, fleeing from His punishment, for your forelocks are in His grip, and you are under His management and disposal.

{135} ﴿Say﴾: O Messenger, to your people, when you have summoned them to God, clarified to them their final end and what is due to Him from them, and they refused to submit to His command, followed their desires, and persisted in their polytheism: ﴿O my people, act according to your position﴾; that is, according to your state in which you are, which you have accepted for yourselves. ﴿Indeed, I am acting﴾ in accordance with God's command and following the pleasure of God. ﴿You will know to whom will belong the final outcome of the abode﴾: me or you. This is a great degree of fairness, in that He clarified the deeds and their doers, and made the recompense accompanied by the perspective of the discerning, leaving aside explicit statement, which is dispensed with by allusion. He knew that the good end in this world and the Hereafter belongs to the righteous, that the believers have the final outcome of the abode, and that every one who turns away from what the messengers brought will have an evil and wretched end. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.﴾ Every wrongdoer, even if he enjoys in this world what he enjoys, his end in it is annihilation and ruin. Indeed, God gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him go.

{128} He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And [mention] the Day He will gather them all together﴾; that is, all of the two weighty beings, mankind and jinn, those who went astray and those who led others astray. Then He will rebuke the jinn who misled mankind, adorned evil for them, and incited them to sins: ﴿O company of jinn, you have led astray a great many of mankind﴾; that is, you have misled them and turned them away from the way of God. How, then, did you dare to violate My sacred prohibitions, defy My messengers, stand as warriors against God, and strive to turn the servants of God away from His way toward the path of Hellfire? ﴿Today, My curse is due upon you, and My retribution is incumbent upon you, and We shall increase you in punishment in accordance with your disbelief and your misguidance of others.﴾ You will have no excuse by which you may apologize, no refuge to which you may flee, no intercessor who will intercede, and no supplication that will be heard. You cannot imagine what will befall them of torment, disgrace, and calamity. For this reason God did not mention any excuse from them. As for their allies among mankind, they presented an excuse that was not accepted. They said: ﴿Our Lord, we benefited from one another﴾; that is, each of the jinn and the human enjoyed the other and profited from him. The jinn enjoyed the human's obedience to him, his worship, his exaltation, and his seeking refuge with him, while the human enjoyed attaining his aims and reaching some of his desires through the service the jinn rendered him. The human worshipped the jinn, the jinn served him, and he obtained for him some worldly needs. ﴿And we have reached our term which You appointed for us﴾; that is, we have arrived at the place where You recompense people for their deeds. So do with us now whatever You will, and judge concerning us as You desire. Our proof has been cut off, we have no excuse left, the command is Yours and the judgment is Yours. In this speech of theirs there appears a kind of humble supplication and softening, but it came at the wrong time. For this reason He judged concerning them with His just judgment, in which there is no injustice, saying: ﴿The Fire is your abode, wherein you will abide forever﴾. Since this judgment was required by His wisdom and His knowledge, He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing﴾. Just as His knowledge encompasses and embraces all things, so His ultimate wisdom includes, embraces, and encompasses all things.

{129} ﴿And thus do We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others, because of what they used to earn﴾; that is, just as We empowered the rebellious jinn and gave them authority to mislead their allies among mankind, and bound them together with the bond of friendship and agreement because of their own earning and striving in that, so too it is part of Our way that We make every wrongdoer an ally of a wrongdoer like himself, who incites him toward evil, urges him to it, makes him averse to good, and repels him from it. This is among the great punishments of God, whose effect is grave and whose danger is profound. The sin belongs to the wrongdoer, for it is he who brought harm upon himself and it is against his own self that he has committed the offense. ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants.﴾
Among this is that when the servants increase in injustice, corruption, and withholding of obligatory rights, they are placed under the rule of oppressors who afflict them with evil torment and take from them, through injustice and tyranny, many times what they withheld from the rights of God and the rights of His servants, without being rewarded or seeking reward for it. Likewise, when the servants become righteous and upright, God makes their rulers righteous and makes them leaders of justice and fairness, not rulers of oppression and tyranny.

{130} Then God rebuked all those among the jinn and mankind who turned away from the truth and rejected it, and clarified their error, and they acknowledged it. He said: ﴿O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses﴾, the clear and manifest signs which contain the details of command and prohibition, good and evil, promise and threat, ﴿and warning you of the meeting of this your Day﴾; that is, teaching you that salvation and success therein come only through complying with God's commands and avoiding His prohibitions, and that wretchedness and loss lie in neglecting that. They acknowledged this and confessed, saying: ﴿Yes.﴾ ﴿We bear witness against ourselves.﴾ ﴿And the worldly life deceived them﴾ with its adornments, its ornaments, and its pleasures, so they were content with it and satisfied, and it diverted them from the Hereafter. ﴿And they bore witness against themselves that they had been disbelievers﴾. Thus the proof of God was established against them, and at that moment everyone, even they themselves, knew the justice of God concerning them. [He said to them, judging them to the painful punishment: Enter into the company of the nations that passed away before you from among the jinn and mankind. They did as you did, enjoyed their share as you enjoyed yours, and plunged into falsehood as you plunged. Indeed they were losers; that is, the former and the latter of these, and what loss is greater than the loss of the Gardens of Bliss and the deprivation of companionship with the Most Noble of the noble?]

{132} But although they share in the loss, they differ greatly in its measure. ﴿And for each are degrees according to what they did﴾; that is, according to their deeds. The one who committed little evil is not treated like the one who committed much, nor is the follower like the leader, nor the subordinate like the chief. Likewise, the people of reward and Paradise, although they share in profit, success, and entry into Paradise, there are among them differences that no one knows but God, and yet they all [have] been pleased with what their Master has given them and content with what He has bestowed. We ask God, the Exalted, to make us among the people of the highest Paradise, which God prepared for the near ones among His servants, the chosen among His creation, and the elite of His friends. ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what they do﴾, so He recompenses each according to his deed and according to what He knows of his intention.

{133} God only commanded His servants to do righteous deeds and forbade them from evil deeds out of mercy toward them and intent for their welfare. Otherwise, He is Self-Sufficient in His essence, independent of all His creation. The obedience of the obedient does not benefit Him, just as the disobedience of the disobedient does not harm Him. ﴿If He wills, He can remove you﴾ by destruction, ﴿and bring after you whom He wills, as He produced you from the descendants of another people.﴾ So when you realize that you must move from this abode as others moved, and depart from it, leaving it for those after you just as those before you departed and left it for you, why then have you taken it as a permanent residence, settled in it, and forgotten that it is a place of passage, not a place of settlement? And [forgotten] that before you is an abode which gathers every bliss and is free of every affliction and defect? It is the abode toward which the former and the latter strive, and toward which the foremost and the latecomers journey. Once they reach it, there is everlasting eternity, lasting residence, the ultimate goal beyond which there is no goal, the sought-after object to which every pursuit comes to an end, and the desired thing before which every desire fades away. There, by God, is what souls desire, what eyes delight in, and what competitors compete for: the pleasure of spirits, abundance of joys, the bliss of bodies and hearts, and nearness to the Knower of the Unseen. So to God belongs a resolve which is attached to those honors, and a will which rises to the highest ranks. How contemptible is the portion of one who is content with the base, and how low is the aspiration of one who chooses the bargain of the deceived!

{134} The heedless one who turns away should not consider the swift arrival of this abode unlikely, for ﴿what you are promised is coming, and you cannot escape﴾ God, fleeing from His punishment, for your forelocks are in His grip, and you are under His management and disposal.

{135} ﴿Say﴾: O Messenger, to your people, when you have summoned them to God, clarified to them their final end and what is due to Him from them, and they refused to submit to His command, followed their desires, and persisted in their polytheism: ﴿O my people, act according to your position﴾; that is, according to your state in which you are, which you have accepted for yourselves. ﴿Indeed, I am acting﴾ in accordance with God's command and following the pleasure of God. ﴿You will know to whom will belong the final outcome of the abode﴾: me or you. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.﴾ Every wrongdoer, even if he enjoys in this world what he enjoys, his end in it is annihilation and ruin. Indeed, God gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him go.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verses 136–140:

{136} Almighty God informs us about the condition of the polytheists who denied the Prophet (ﷺ): their foolishness of intellect, levity of mind, and profound ignorance. God, blessed and exalted, enumerates some of their superstitions in order to alert [the reader] to their misguidance and to the need to be wary of them, and [to show] that the opposition of such foolish people to the truth brought by the Messenger does not in any way detract from it, for they have no competence to stand against the truth. Among what He mentions of this is that they:{assigned to God} a share {of the produce and the cattle which He has created}: and for their associates they assigned a share of it, while in fact God Most High is the One who created it for the servants and brought it into being as provision. Thus they combined two prohibited matters, indeed three violations:
First, their presumption upon God in assigning Him a share while believing that this was a voluntary act of their own.
Second, associating with Him partners who had neither provided for them nor brought anything into being for them in this.
Third, their unjust judgment: what belonged to God they did not care for or pay attention to, but if it reached their associates, which was not theirs [to give], they took great care of it and guarded it, and nothing of it reached God. This is because, when they obtained some of their crops, fruits, and livestock, which God had brought into being for them, they divided it into two parts: one part they said was "for God," by their claim and assumption, and otherwise God accepts only what is sincerely for His sake and does not accept the deed of one who associates others with Him; and the other part they made the portion of their partners, the idols and rivals. If something of what they had assigned to God reached what they had assigned to others and got mixed with it, they did not mind, saying, "God is independent of it," so they did not return it; but if something of what they had assigned to their gods reached what they had assigned to God, they returned it to its place, saying, "They are poor, and the portion of them must be returned." Is there any judgment worse or more unjust than this, in which they made what belongs to a created being something they strive over, advise about, and guard more than what they do for the right of God?
It is possible that the meaning of this noble verse is what is established in the "Sahih" from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said, relating from God, that He said: "I am the most independent of partners from association; whoever associates something with Me, I leave him and his association." And the meaning of the verse is that what they assigned and drew near to by way of their idols is a pure drawing near to other than God, of which God has no share; and what they assigned to God by their claim, it does not reach Him, because it is association, but rather it becomes the portion of the partners and rivals, since God is independent of it and does not accept the deed in which anyone among creation has associated with Him.

{137} And among the foolishness and misguidance of the polytheists is that {their partners made attractive to many of the polytheists} — that is, their chiefs and their devils — the killing of their children, namely burying alive, by which they bury their children out of fear of poverty, and females out of fear of shame. All of this is among the deceptions of the devils, who wish to lead them to destruction and to confuse their religion for them, so they commit acts of the utmost ugliness; and their partners continue to adorn these for them until they become, in their eyes, among the good matters and praiseworthy qualities. Had God willed to prevent them and to come between them and these acts, and to prevent their children from being killed by their parents, they would not have done it. But His wisdom required that He leave them to their own actions, as a means of gradual leading [to ruin] and a respite for them, and out of His indifference to what they are upon. For this reason He said: {So leave them and what they fabricate}; that is, leave them with their lying and their fabrication, and do not grieve over them, for they will never harm God in the least.

{138} And among the kinds of their foolishness is that the livestock which God made lawful for them in general, and made a provision and a mercy from which they benefit and enjoy, they have invented innovations and statements of their own accord. Among them is a convention regarding some livestock and crops, in which they say: {These are livestock and crops, forbidden}; that is, prohibited. {None may eat of them except whom we wish}; that is, it is not permitted for anyone to eat of them except one whom we want to feed, or whom we describe by a description of our own choosing. All of this, by their claim, has no basis or proof for them except their desires and their corrupt opinions.
And [there are] livestock that are not forbidden in every respect, but they forbid their backs; that is, by riding them and loading them, and they protect their backs, and they call them the *hām*.
And [there are] livestock over which they do not mention the name of God, but instead mention the names of their idols and what they worshipped besides God over them, and they attribute those practices to God, while they are liars and wicked in that. {He will repay them for what they used to fabricate}: against God, by making lawful association and forbidding what is lawful of food and benefits.

{139} And among their feeble opinions is that they make some livestock, specifying them, as forbidden, and what is in their wombs forbidden to females but not to males. They say: {What is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males}; that is, lawful for them, with no women sharing in it. {And forbidden to our wives}; that is, to our women. This applies if it is born alive; but if what is in its womb is born dead, then they share in it; that is, it is lawful for both males and females. {He will repay them} God {for their description}: in that they described what God had made lawful as forbidden, and described the forbidden as lawful, thus contradicting the law of God, opposing it, and attributing that to God. {Indeed He is Wise}: in that He granted them respite and empowered them in the misguidance they are in. {All-Knowing}: nothing about them is hidden from Him; He knows them and what they said and fabricated against Him, and He pardons them and provides for them, exalted is His majesty.

{140} Then He made clear their loss and the foolishness of their intellects, saying: {Those have lost who killed their children in foolishness without knowledge}; that is, they lost their religion, their children, and their intellects, and their description after sound intellects became deluded foolishness and misguidance. {And have forbidden what God has provided them}; that is, what He made a mercy for them and sent as provision for them. They rejected the generosity of their Lord, and were not content with that, but described it as forbidden, while it is among the most lawful of lawful things. All of this is {a fabrication against God}; that is, a lie by which every obstinate disbeliever lies. {They have gone astray and were not guided}; that is, they went far astray, and were not guided in any of their affairs.

Thus they combined two prohibited matters, indeed three violations:
First, their presumption upon God in assigning Him a share while believing that this was a voluntary act of their own.
Second, associating with Him partners who had neither provided for them nor brought anything into being for them in this.
Third, their unjust judgment: what belonged to God they did not care for or pay attention to, but if it reached their associates, which was not theirs [to give], they took great care of it and guarded it, and nothing of it reached God. This is because, when they obtained some of their crops, fruits, and livestock, which God had brought into being for them, they divided it into two parts: one part they said was "for God," by their claim and assumption, and otherwise God accepts only what is sincerely for His sake and does not accept the deed of one who associates others with Him; and the other part they made the portion of their partners, the idols and rivals. If something of what they had assigned to God reached what they had assigned to others and got mixed with it, they did not mind, saying, "God is independent of it," so they did not return it; but if something of what they had assigned to their gods reached what they had assigned to God, they returned it to its place, saying, "They are poor, and the portion of them must be returned." Is there any judgment worse or more unjust than this, in which they made what belongs to a created being something they strive over, advise about, and guard more than what they do for the right of God?
It is possible that the meaning of this noble verse is what is established in the "Sahih" from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said, relating from God, that He said: "I am the most independent of partners from association; whoever associates something with Me, I leave him and his association." And the meaning of the verse is that what they assigned and drew near to by way of their idols is a pure drawing near to other than God, of which God has no share; and what they assigned to God by their claim, it does not reach Him, because it is association, but rather it becomes the portion of the partners and rivals, since God is independent of it and does not accept the deed in which anyone among creation has associated with Him.

{137} And among the foolishness and misguidance of the polytheists is that {their partners made attractive to many of the polytheists} — that is, their chiefs and their devils — the killing of their children, namely burying alive, by which they bury their children out of fear of poverty, and females out of fear of shame. All of this is among the deceptions of the devils, who wish to lead them to destruction and to confuse their religion for them, so they commit acts of the utmost ugliness; and their partners continue to adorn these for them until they become, in their eyes, among the good matters and praiseworthy qualities. Had God willed to prevent them and to come between them and these acts, and to prevent their children from being killed by their parents, they would not have done it. But His wisdom required that He leave them to their own actions, as a means of gradual leading [to ruin] and a respite for them, and out of His indifference to what they are upon. For this reason He said: {So leave them and what they fabricate}; that is, leave them with their lying and their fabrication, and do not grieve over them, for they will never harm God in the least.

{138} And among the kinds of their foolishness is that the livestock which God made lawful for them in general, and made a provision and a mercy from which they benefit and enjoy, they have invented innovations and statements of their own accord. Among them is a convention regarding some livestock and crops, in which they say: {These are livestock and crops, forbidden}; that is, prohibited. {None may eat of them except whom we wish}; that is, it is not permitted for anyone to eat of them except one whom we want to feed, or whom we describe by a description of our own choosing. All of this, by their claim, has no basis or proof for them except their desires and their corrupt opinions.
And [there are] livestock that are not forbidden in every respect, but they forbid their backs; that is, by riding them and loading them, and they protect their backs, and they call them the *hām*.
And [there are] livestock over which they do not mention the name of God, but instead mention the names of their idols and what they worshipped besides God over them, and they attribute those practices to God, while they are liars and wicked in that. {He will repay them for what they used to fabricate}: against God, by making lawful association and forbidding what is lawful of food and benefits.

{139} And among their feeble opinions is that they make some livestock, specifying them, as forbidden, and what is in their wombs forbidden to females but not to males. They say: {What is in the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males}; that is, lawful for them, with no women sharing in it. {And forbidden to our wives}; that is, to our women. This applies if it is born alive; but if what is in its womb is born dead, then they share in it; that is, it is lawful for both males and females. {He will repay them} God {for their description}: in that they described what God had made lawful as forbidden, and described the forbidden as lawful, thus contradicting the law of God, opposing it, and attributing that to God. {Indeed He is Wise}: in that He granted them respite and empowered them in the misguidance they are in. {All-Knowing}: nothing about them is hidden from Him; He knows them and what they said and fabricated against Him, and He pardons them and provides for them, exalted is His majesty.

{140} Then He made clear their loss and the foolishness of their intellects, saying: {Those have lost who killed their children in foolishness without knowledge}; that is, they lost their religion, their children, and their intellects, and their description after sound intellects became deluded foolishness and misguidance. {And have forbidden what God has provided them}; that is, what He made a mercy for them and sent as provision for them. They rejected the generosity of their Lord, and were not content with that, but described it as forbidden, while it is among the most lawful of lawful things. All of this is {a fabrication against God}; that is, a lie by which every obstinate disbeliever lies. {They have gone astray and were not guided}; that is, they went far astray, and were not guided in any of their affairs.
