{141} When Allah mentioned the handling by the polytheists of much of what Allah had made lawful to them of crops and livestock, He, blessed and exalted is He, mentioned His favour upon them in that, and their obligation that is binding upon them regarding crops and livestock, so He said: ﴿And it is He who produced gardens﴾; that is, orchards containing various kinds of trees and differing plants, ﴿trellised and untrellised﴾; that is, some of those gardens have trellises made for them upon which the trees spread and which assist them in rising up from the ground, and some are free of trellises, growing upon a stalk or spreading out on the ground. In this there is an indication of the abundance of their benefits and goodness, and that Allah, exalted is He, taught the servants how to trellis them and cause them to grow. ﴿And﴾ He produced ﴿the palm trees and crops, varying in their produce﴾; that is, its produce is in one place and drinks from one water, yet Allah makes some of it excel others in food. Allah singled out palm trees and crops of its various kinds for the abundance of their benefits and because they are the sustenance of most of creation. ﴿And﴾ He produced ﴿the olive and the pomegranate, resembling one another﴾ in their trees, ﴿and not resembling﴾ in their fruit and taste. It is as if it were said: For what did Allah produce these gardens, and what is joined to them? So He informed that He produced them for the benefits of the servants, and said: ﴿Eat of its fruit﴾; that is, of the palm trees and crops, ﴿when it bears fruit, and give its due on the day of its harvest﴾; that is, give the due of the crops, which is the zakat with its prescribed portions in the Sharia. He commanded them to give it on the day of its harvest, because the harvesting of crops is equivalent to the passing of a year, since it is the time toward which the souls of the poor are eager, and bringing it out is then easy for the people of the crops, and the matter concerning it is evident to the one who gives it, so that the giver is distinguished from the one who does not give.

And His saying: ﴿And do not be excessive﴾ encompasses the prohibition of excess in eating, which is exceeding the limit and custom, and that the owner of the crop eats in a way that harms the zakat, and excess in bringing out the due of the crop, such that he gives more than what is obligatory upon him, or that he harms himself, his dependents, or his creditors. All of this is from the excess which Allah has forbidden, which He does not love, but rather hates, and is wrathful toward.

In this verse there is evidence for the obligation of zakat on fruits, and that they have no hawl (lunar year); rather, their hawl is their harvest in crops and the gathering of dates from palm trees. It is also evidence that zakat is not repeated on them if they remain with the servant for many years, provided they are not for trade, because Allah only commanded their payment at the time of their harvest. It is also evidence that if a calamity befalls them before that, without negligence on the part of the owner of the crop and fruit, he is not liable for them. It is also evidence that it is permissible to eat from the palm trees and crops before paying zakat on them, and that this is not counted toward the zakat; rather, he pays zakat on the wealth that remains after it. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to send an estimator (kharis) who would estimate people's fruit for them, and he would instruct him to leave for its owners a third or a quarter, according to what is consumed from it by its owners and others.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verse 142–144:

{142} That is: {And} He created and produced {of the cattle, some for burden and some for meat}; meaning, some of them you use for carrying loads and riding, and some are not fit for carrying and riding because of their small size, such as the young camels (al-fuslan) and the like, and these are the "farsh" (the ones for meat). So, in terms of carrying and riding, they divide into these two categories. As for eating and various kinds of benefit, all of them may be eaten and benefited from, and for this reason He said: {Eat of what Allah has provided for you and do not follow the steps of Satan}; meaning, his paths and works, among which is that you forbid some of what Allah has provided for you. {Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy}: so he does not command you except with what harms you and brings you everlasting misery.

{143} These cattle, with which Allah has favored His servants and which He made entirely lawful and good, He detailed as: {eight mates: of sheep two and of goats two}: a male and a female, {and of goats two}: likewise. These are four, all of which are included in what Allah has made lawful, with no distinction between any of them. So say to those who presumptuously forbid some of them and not others, or who forbid some of them to females and not males, binding them to the absence of any distinction between what they have permitted from them and what they have forbidden: {the two males}: of the sheep and the goats, {has He forbidden}: Allah? You do not say this and apply it consistently. {Or the two females}: has Allah forbidden from the sheep and the goats? This is not your view either, neither forbidding the pure males nor the pure females of the two kinds. There remains the case where the womb contains a male and a female, or something unknown, so He said: {Or}: do you forbid {what the wombs of the two females contain}; meaning, the female of the sheep and the female of the goat, without distinction between male and female. You do not say this either. So if you do not hold to any of these three positions, which exhaust all possible divisions in this matter, then to what will you turn? {Inform me with knowledge, if you are truthful}: in your saying and your claim.

It is well known that they cannot state any view that is rationally acceptable except one of these three, and they hold none of them. Rather, they say that some of the cattle, which they have designated by conventions of their own invention, are forbidden to females but not to males, or forbidden at certain times, or similar statements, whose origin is known with certainty to be compound ignorance, deranged and deviant minds, and corrupt opinions, and that Allah has not sent down any authority for what they say, nor do they have any proof or argument for it.

{144} Then He mentioned the same regarding camels and cattle. When He clarified the invalidity and corruption of their view, He said to them a statement from which they have no way to escape its consequence except by following the law of Allah: {Or were you witnesses when Allah enjoined this upon you}; meaning, nothing remains for you except a claim for which you have no way to establish its truth and soundness, namely that you say: Allah enjoined this upon us and revealed it to us as He revealed to His messengers. Rather, He revealed to us a revelation contrary to what the messengers called to and what the books came with. This is a fabrication that no one is ignorant of. For this reason He said: {Who is more unjust than one who invents a lie against Allah to mislead people without knowledge}; meaning, along with his lying and fabrication against Allah, his aim thereby is to [mislead] the servants of Allah from the way of Allah, without any clear evidence from Him, nor proof, nor reason, nor transmission. {Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people}: those who have no desire except for injustice, oppression, and fabrication against Allah.

**{145}** When the Exalted mentioned the blame of the polytheists for what they had made unlawful of the lawful, attributing it to God, and nullified their claim, He commanded His Messenger to make clear to the people what God had made unlawful for them, so that they would know that whatever is other than that is lawful, and that whoever attributes its prohibition to God is a liar and a nullifier, because prohibition can only come from God, through the tongue of His Messenger. And He said to His Messenger: ﴿Say, "I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who eats, except that it be dead meat, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is impure, or a grave sin, that which has been dedicated to other than God."﴾ That is, forbidden to eat, setting aside the question of whether using anything other than eating is forbidden or not. "Except that it be dead meat": carrion is what has died without lawful slaughter (dhakah shar'iyyah), and that is not lawful, as the Exalted said: ﴿Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine﴾. "Or blood poured forth": this is the blood that flows from the slaughtered animal at its slaughter, for it is the blood whose retention in the body is harmful; when it has flowed out of the body, the harm is removed by eating the meat.

The implication of this wording is that the blood which remains in the flesh and the veins after slaughter is lawful and pure. "Or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is impure": that is, these three things are impure (rijs), meaning filthy, unclean and harmful, which God has forbidden out of kindness to you and to keep you pure from approaching what is foul. "Or": except that it be ﴿a grave sin, that which has been dedicated to other than God﴾. That is, except that the animal has been slaughtered for other than God, for idols and deities worshipped by the polytheists; for this is a sin (fisq), which is departing from obedience to God into disobedience. Along with this, these forbidden things are permitted to one who is compelled by necessity, that is, who is driven by need and dire necessity to eat some of them, having nothing else and fearing for his life, ﴿neither willful nor transgressing﴾. That is, not desiring to eat them without necessity, and not exceeding the limit, by eating more than his need. ﴿But whoever is compelled, neither willful nor transgressing, indeed your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: that is, God has pardoned the one in this condition.

The scholars, may God have mercy on them, differed concerning the restriction stated in this verse, given that there are other prohibitions not mentioned in it, such as beasts of prey and every bird with talons, and the like. Some said: this verse was revealed before the prohibition of what was added beyond what is mentioned in it, so this restriction does not conflict with the later prohibition, since he had not found it in what was revealed to him at that time.

Others said: this verse encompasses all the prohibitions, some explicitly and some derived from its meaning and the general cause, for His saying regarding the cause of carrion, blood and swine flesh (or only the last of them): ﴿for indeed it is impure﴾ is a description encompassing every prohibited thing, since all prohibited things are impure and foul, and they are among the repugnant foulnesses which God has forbidden to His servants, to protect and honour them from contact with the foul and impure. The details of the forbidden impurity are taken from the Sunnah, for it explains the Qur'an and makes clear its intent.

Since God has not prohibited any food except what is mentioned, and prohibition can only originate from the law of God, this shows that the polytheists who forbade what God had provided for them are liars against God, fabricating against Him what He did not say.

This verse has a strong possibility (of another meaning), were it not that God mentioned swine in it: that the context is the refutation of the earlier claims of the polytheists regarding their prohibition of what God had made lawful, and their plunging into this according to what their souls had embellished for them, and that this concerns especially the grazing livestock, of which only what is mentioned in the verse is prohibited: carrion, and that which is dedicated to other than God; and all else is lawful. Perhaps the reason for mentioning swine here, on this possibility, is that some ignorant people may include it among the grazing livestock, thinking it a kind of sheep, as the ignorant among the Christians and their like may imagine; so they raise it as they raise livestock, consider it lawful, and make no distinction between it and the cattle.

**{146}** So what is forbidden to this entire nation is by way of purification and protection for them. As for what was forbidden to the People of the Book, some of it is good, but it was forbidden to them as a punishment, and therefore He said: ﴿And to those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws﴾: such as camels and the like. And We forbade them some parts of the cattle and sheep, namely their fats, though not all fats were forbidden, but only the fat of the kidneys and the caul; this is why He excepted the lawful fat from that, saying: ﴿except what their backs carry or the entrails, or what is mixed with bone﴾; that is, the fat mixed with the intestines (al-hawaya). ﴿That is what We requited them for their rebellion﴾: that is, their injustice and transgression against the rights of God and the rights of His servants, so God forbade them these things as a punishment and a chastisement. ﴿And indeed We are truthful﴾ in all that We say, do and judge; and who is more truthful in statement than God? And who is better in judgment than God for a people who are certain?

**{145}** When the Exalted mentioned the blame of the polytheists for what they had made unlawful of the lawful, attributing it to God, and nullified their claim, He commanded His Messenger to make clear to the people what God had made unlawful for them, so that they would know that whatever is other than that is lawful, and that whoever attributes its prohibition to God is a liar and a nullifier, because prohibition can only come from God, through the tongue of His Messenger. And He said to His Messenger: ﴿Say, "I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who eats, except that it be dead meat, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is impure, or a grave sin, that which has been dedicated to other than God."﴾ That is, forbidden to eat, setting aside the question of whether using anything other than eating is forbidden or not. "Except that it be dead meat": carrion is what has died without lawful slaughter (dhakah shar'iyyah), and that is not lawful, as the Exalted said: ﴿Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine﴾. "Or blood poured forth": this is the blood that flows from the slaughtered animal at its slaughter, for it is the blood whose retention in the body is harmful; when it has flowed out of the body, the harm is removed by eating the meat.

The implication of this wording is that the blood which remains in the flesh and the veins after slaughter is lawful and pure. "Or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is impure": that is, these three things are impure (rijs), meaning filthy, unclean and harmful, which God has forbidden out of kindness to you and to keep you pure from approaching what is foul. "Or": except that it be ﴿a grave sin, that which has been dedicated to other than God﴾. That is, except that the animal has been slaughtered for other than God, for idols and deities worshipped by the polytheists; for this is a sin (fisq), which is departing from obedience to God into disobedience. Along with this, these forbidden things are permitted to one who is compelled by necessity, that is, who is driven by need and dire necessity to eat some of them, having nothing else and fearing for his life, ﴿neither willful nor transgressing﴾. That is, not desiring to eat them without necessity, and not exceeding the limit, by eating more than his need. ﴿But whoever is compelled, neither willful nor transgressing, indeed your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: that is, God has pardoned the one in this condition.

The scholars, may God have mercy on them, differed concerning the restriction stated in this verse, given that there are other prohibitions not mentioned in it, such as beasts of prey and every bird with talons, and the like. Some said: this verse was revealed before the prohibition of what was added beyond what is mentioned in it, so this restriction does not conflict with the later prohibition, since he had not found it in what was revealed to him at that time.

Others said: this verse encompasses all the prohibitions, some explicitly and some derived from its meaning and the general cause, for His saying regarding the cause of carrion, blood and swine flesh (or only the last of them): ﴿for indeed it is impure﴾ is a description encompassing every prohibited thing, since all prohibited things are impure and foul, and they are among the repugnant foulnesses which God has forbidden to His servants, to protect and honour them from contact with the foul and impure. The details of the forbidden impurity are taken from the Sunnah, for it explains the Qur'an and makes clear its intent.

Since God has not prohibited any food except what is mentioned, and prohibition can only originate from the law of God, this shows that the polytheists who forbade what God had provided for them are liars against God, fabricating against Him what He did not say.

This verse has a strong possibility (of another meaning), were it not that God mentioned swine in it: that the context is the refutation of the earlier claims of the polytheists regarding their prohibition of what God had made lawful, and their plunging into this according to what their souls had embellished for them, and that this concerns especially the grazing livestock, of which only what is mentioned in the verse is prohibited: carrion, and that which is dedicated to other than God; and all else is lawful. And who is better in judgment than God for a people who are certain?

{147} That is: if these polytheists deny you, then persist in calling them to it through encouragement and warning, and inform them that Allah is ﴿Possessor of vast mercy﴾; that is, it is general and encompassing of all created beings. So hasten toward His mercy through its causes, whose head, foundation and substance is the affirmation of Muhammad (ﷺ) in what he brought. ﴿And His punishment will not be turned away from the criminal people﴾; that is, those whose crimes and sins have multiplied. So beware of the crimes that lead to Allah's punishment, the greatest and foremost of which is denying Muhammad (ﷺ).

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verse 148–149:

{148} This is information from God that the polytheists will argue for their polytheism and their prohibition of what God has made lawful by appeal to divine decree and predestination (al-qada' wa'l-qadar), and they will make God's will, which encompasses every good and evil, a proof for themselves in order to avert blame from themselves. They have indeed said what God informed that they would say, as He said in another verse: ﴿And those who associated others with God say: "Had God willed, we would not have worshipped anything besides Him, neither we nor our fathers, nor would we have prohibited anything without [authority]."﴾ ... [to the end of the verse]. He, exalted is He, informed that this argument has not ceased to be used by the denying nations to avert from themselves the call of the messengers, and they argue with it, yet it did not benefit them or avail them anything. This remained their custom until God destroyed them and made them taste His might. So if it were a sound argument, it would have averted punishment from them, and God would not have sent down the torment upon them, for His might does not descend except upon one who deserves it. Thus it is known that it is a corrupt argument and a worthless doubt, for several reasons:
Among them: what God mentioned, that if it were sound, punishment would not have befallen them.
Among them: that an argument must be grounded in knowledge and proof. As for when it is grounded in mere conjecture and guesswork, which does not avail anything against the truth, then it is void. For this reason He said: ﴿Say: "Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us?"﴾ Had they possessed knowledge, and they are fierce adversaries, they would have produced it. Since they did not produce it, it is known that they have no knowledge. ﴿You follow nothing but conjecture, and you are only guessing.﴾ Whoever builds his arguments on guesswork and conjecture is a false and losing party; how much more so if he builds them on rebellion, obstinacy, evil and corruption.

{149} Among them: the argument belongs to God, the conclusive one, which has left no excuse for anyone, upon which the prophets and messengers, the divine books, the prophetic traditions, sound intellects, upright natures and sound morals all agree. Thus it is known that whatever contradicts this decisive verse is false, for the opposite of truth can only be falsehood.
Among them: God, exalted is He, gave every creature power and will by which it is able to do what it has been charged with. God does not obligate anyone to do what he cannot do, nor does He forbid anyone what he cannot avoid. Therefore, invoking decree and predestination after this is pure injustice and sheer obstinacy.
Among them: God, exalted is He, did not compel the servants to their actions; rather He made their actions follow their choice. If they wish, they act, and if they wish, they refrain. This is an observed matter that none denies except one who is obstinate and denies what is perceived by the senses, for everyone distinguishes between voluntary movement (al-harakah al-ikhtiyariyyah) and involuntary movement (al-harakah al-qasriyyah), even though all of it falls within God's will and is subsumed under His determination.
Among them: those who argue for sins by decree and predestination contradict themselves in this, for they cannot apply it consistently. Indeed, if someone wronged them by beating them, taking their property, or the like, and argued by decree and predestination, they would not accept that argument from him and would be angered by it in the extreme. How strange it is that they argue with it for disobedience to God and what displeases Him, yet they do not accept from anyone that he argue with it against what displeases them.
Among them: their argument by decree and predestination is not sincerely intended; they know that it is not a proof. Its real purpose is to repel the truth, and they regard the truth as an attacker, so they repel it with whatever words come to mind, [even though they believe it to be wrong].

{150} That is: say to those who have forbidden what God has made lawful and attributed that to God: "Bring forward your witnesses who testify that God has forbidden this!" If they are told this, they are caught between two matters. Either they fail to bring anyone who testifies to this, in which case their claim is then false, devoid of witnesses and proof. Or they bring someone who testifies for them to that, but none can testify to this except every liar, sinner, whose testimony is not accepted, and this is not one of the matters on which the upright (ʿudul) may validly testify. For this reason, God, the Exalted, forbade His Prophet and his followers from such testimony, saying: ﴿So if they testify, do not testify with them, and do not follow the desires of those who deny Our signs and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and who make equals to their Lord﴾; that is, they ascribe to Him equals from other deities and idols. Since they disbelieve in the Last Day and do not affirm the oneness of God, their desires are suited to their creed and revolve between polytheism and denial of the truth. It is fitting that God forbid the best of His creation from following a desire of this nature and from testifying along with its adherents. It is then known that their forbidding what God has made lawful proceeds from those misguiding desires.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verses 151–153:

{151} The Exalted says to His Prophet ﷺ: {Say}: to those who have forbidden what Allah has made lawful: {Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you}: a general and comprehensive prohibition for everyone, encompassing all forbidden things, of foods, drinks, words and deeds. {That you associate nothing with Him}; that is, not a little and not a lot. The reality of associating partners with Allah (shirk) is that a created being is worshipped as Allah is worshipped, or is magnified as Allah is magnified, or some kind of the specific attributes of lordship and divinity is directed to it. When the servant abandons all of shirk, he becomes one who affirms the oneness of Allah and is sincere to Him in all his states. This is the right of Allah over His servants: that they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him. Then he began with the most emphatic of rights after His right, saying: {And to parents, good treatment}: in gracious words and beautiful, commendable deeds. Every word and deed by which benefit or joy comes to the parents is part of good treatment, and when good treatment exists, disobedience (ʿuquq) is absent. {And do not kill your children}: whether males or females {out of poverty}; that is, because of destitution and your constraint regarding their provision, as was present in the cruel and oppressive pre-Islamic period (al-Jahiliyyah). If they are forbidden from killing them in this state, while they are their own children, then forbidding the killing of them without a just cause, or the killing of the children of others, is all the more fitting and proper. {We provide for you and for them}; that is, We have already guaranteed the provision of all, so you are not the ones who provide for your children, nor even for yourselves, so there is no constraint upon you on their account. {And do not approach the immoralities}: which are the great, abominable sins {what is apparent of them and what is concealed}; that is, do not approach the outward of them and the hidden, or what relates to the outward and what relates to the heart and inner self. The prohibition against approaching immoralities is more emphatic than the prohibition against merely committing them, for it encompasses the prohibition of their preliminaries and the means that lead to them. {And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden}: and this is the soul of a Muslim, male or female, young or old, pious or wicked, and the disbelieving soul which is protected by covenant and pact, {except by right}: such as a married adulterer, a life for a life, and one who abandons his religion and separates from the community. {That is what He has enjoined upon you}, the aforementioned, {[that] He has enjoined upon you that you may use your reason}: concerning Allah's command, then preserve it, then observe it and uphold it. The verse indicates that the extent of the servant's upholding of what Allah has commanded is according to the servant's intellect.

{152} {And do not approach the property of the orphan}: by consuming it, or by an exchange conducted in a manner of favoritism to yourselves, or by taking it without a cause, {except in the way that is best}; that is, except in the condition by which their wealth is improved and they benefit from it. This indicates that it is not permissible to approach it or to dispose of it in a manner that harms the orphans, or in a manner that involves neither harm nor benefit. {Until he reaches his maturity (ashuddahu)}: that is, until he reaches adulthood, becomes mature in judgment, and knows how to manage affairs. When he reaches his maturity, his wealth is given to him at that time, and he disposes of it according to his own judgment. This indicates that the orphan before reaching maturity is under guardianship, that his guardian manages his property in the best interest, and that this guardianship ends upon reaching maturity. {And give full measure and weight in justice}; that is, with justice and complete fulfilment. When you strive in that, then {We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity}; that is, according to what it can bear and is not strained by. So whoever is keen to give full measure and weight, and then some shortfall occurs from him without his negligence or knowledge, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. The usuliyyun (scholars of the principles of jurisprudence) have derived from this verse [and similar ones] that Allah does not burden anyone with what they cannot bear, and that whoever fears Allah in what He has commanded and does what he is able to do of it, there is no blame upon him for what lies beyond that. {And when you speak}: a word by which you judge among people, decide between them in speech, and speak concerning matters and circumstances, {then be just}: in your speech, by observing truthfulness regarding those you love and those you dislike, and by fairness and not concealing what must be made clear. For inclining against one you dislike in speech about him or his statement is a forbidden injustice. Rather, when a scholar speaks about the doctrines of the people of innovation (ahl al-bidʿah), it is obligatory upon him to give everyone his right and to make clear what in them is truth and falsehood, considering how close they are to the truth and how far from it. The jurists have mentioned that a judge must be just between the two litigants in his glance and in his speech. {And fulfil the covenant of Allah}: this includes the covenant which the servants have made with Him, of upholding His rights and fulfilling them, and the covenant that is made between creatures; all of it must be fulfilled, and breaking it or neglecting it is forbidden. {That is what He has enjoined upon you}: the rulings mentioned, {[that] He has enjoined upon you that you may remember}: what He has made clear to you of rulings, and that you may uphold Allah's command to you in the fullest manner, and know what wisdom and rulings it contains.

{153} When He had made clear many of the great commands and the important laws, He pointed to them and to what is more general than them, saying: {And that this is My path, [being] straight}; that is, these rulings and what resembles them, of what Allah has made clear in His Book and explained to His servants, are the path of Allah which leads to Him and to the abode of His honour, moderate, easy and concise. {So follow it}: that you may attain success and salvation, and reach hopes and joys. {And do not follow the [other] paths}; that is, the ways that oppose this way, {lest they separate you from His way}; that is, they lead you astray from it and scatter you to the right and left. So when you go astray from the straight path, there is nothing but paths that lead to the Hellfire. {That is what He has enjoined upon you that you may become righteous}: for when you uphold what Allah has made clear to you, in knowledge and action, you become among the righteous and the successful servants of Allah. He made the path singular and attributed it to Himself because it is a single way that leads to Him, and Allah is the One who helps those who travel upon it to traverse it.

The verse indicates that the extent of the servant's upholding of what Allah has commanded is according to the servant's intellect.

{152} {And do not approach the property of the orphan}: by consuming it, or by an exchange conducted in a manner of favoritism to yourselves, or by taking it without a cause, {except in the way that is best}; that is, except in the condition by which their wealth is improved and they benefit from it. This indicates that it is not permissible to approach it or to dispose of it in a manner that harms the orphans, or in a manner that involves neither harm nor benefit. {Until he reaches his maturity (ashuddahu)}: that is, until he reaches adulthood, becomes mature in judgment, and knows how to manage affairs. When he reaches his maturity, his wealth is given to him at that time, and he disposes of it according to his own judgment. This indicates that the orphan before reaching maturity is under guardianship, that his guardian manages his property in the best interest, and that this guardianship ends upon reaching maturity. {And give full measure and weight in justice}; that is, with justice and complete fulfilment. When you strive in that, then {We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity}; that is, according to what it can bear and is not strained by. So whoever is keen to give full measure and weight, and then some shortfall occurs from him without his negligence or knowledge, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. The usuliyyun (scholars of the principles of jurisprudence) have derived from this verse [and similar ones] that Allah does not burden anyone with what they cannot bear, and that whoever fears Allah in what He has commanded and does what he is able to do of it, there is no blame upon him for what lies beyond that. {And when you speak}: a word by which you judge among people, decide between them in speech, and speak concerning matters and circumstances, {then be just}: in your speech, by observing truthfulness regarding those you love and those you dislike, and by fairness and not concealing what must be made clear. For inclining against one you dislike in speech about him or his statement is a forbidden injustice. Rather, when a scholar speaks about the doctrines of the people of innovation (ahl al-bidʿah), it is obligatory upon him to give everyone his right and to make clear what in them is truth and falsehood, considering how close they are to the truth and how far from it. The jurists have mentioned that a judge must be just between the two litigants in his glance and in his speech. {And fulfil the covenant of Allah}: this includes the covenant which the servants have made with Him, of upholding His rights and fulfilling them, and the covenant that is made between creatures; all of it must be fulfilled, and breaking it or neglecting it is forbidden. {That is what He has enjoined upon you}: the rulings mentioned, {[that] He has enjoined upon you that you may remember}: what He has made clear to you of rulings, and that you may uphold Allah's command to you in the fullest manner, and know what wisdom and rulings it contains.

{153} When He had made clear many of the great commands and the important laws, He pointed to them and to what is more general than them, saying: {And that this is My path, [being] straight}; that is, these rulings and what resembles them, of what Allah has made clear in His Book and explained to His servants, are the path of Allah which leads to Him and to the abode of His honour, moderate, easy and concise. {So follow it}: that you may attain success and salvation, and reach hopes and joys. {And do not follow the [other] paths}; that is, the ways that oppose this way, {lest they separate you from His way}; that is, they lead you astray from it and scatter you to the right and left. So when you go astray from the straight path, there is nothing but paths that lead to the Hellfire. {That is what He has enjoined upon you that you may become righteous}: for when you uphold what Allah has made clear to you, in knowledge and action, you become among the righteous and the successful servants of Allah. {154} "Thumma" (then) in this place does not mean chronological sequence, for the time of Musa (peace be upon him) precedes the recitation of this Book by the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). {158} He, exalted is He, says: Are these people, whose wrongdoing and obstinacy have persisted, waiting {except that there come to them} the preliminaries of punishment and the preliminaries of the Hereafter: that {the angels} come to them to take their souls. For when they reach that state, neither faith nor righteous deeds will benefit them. {Or your Lord comes}: to decide judgment between the servants and to recompense the good-doers and the evildoers. {Or some of the signs of your Lord come}: those indicating the nearness of the Hour. {On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come}: the signs that break the normal course of things, by which it is known that the Hour has drawn near and the Resurrection has approached. {No soul will benefit from its faith if it had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith.} That is: when some of God's signs appear, faith will not benefit the disbeliever if he believes, nor will it benefit the believer who was negligent that his good increases after that. Rather, what benefits him is the faith he had before that and the good that existed in him before some of the signs came. The wisdom in this is evident: faith benefits only when it is faith in the unseen and is a choice made by the servant. But when the signs appear, the matter becomes witnessed, and faith no longer has any benefit, for it resembles compelled faith, like the faith of the drowning person and the one caught in fire, and others like them, who, when they see death, abandon what they were doing. As God, exalted is He, says: {So when they saw Our might, they said: "We believe in God alone, and we disbelieve in what we used to associate with Him." But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might. This is the way of God which has passed among His servants.}

Many sound hadiths have been transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) that what is meant by "some of the signs of God" is the rising of the sun from its west, and that when people see it, they will believe, but their faith will not benefit them, and the door of repentance will then be closed. Since this was a threat, awaited by those who denied the Messenger (ﷺ), while they were waiting for the Prophet (ﷺ) and his followers to suffer the calamities of time and the afflictions of affairs, He said: {Say: "Wait, indeed we are waiting."} Soon you will know which of us is more deserving of security.

In this verse there is evidence for the position of the People of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah on affirming the voluntary actions of God, such as His istiwa' (settling), descent, and coming, exalted is He, without likening Him to the attributes of created beings. The Book and the Sunnah contain much of this.

It also indicates that the rising of the sun from the west is among the minor signs of the Hour.

And that God, the Wise, has a established custom and practice that faith benefits only when it is voluntary, not compelled, as has already been mentioned. And that a person gains good through his faith: obedience, righteousness and piety benefit and grow only when faith is present in the servant. When the heart is empty of faith, nothing of that benefits it.

{159} He threatens those who split up their religion; that is, who fragmented it and divided into factions within it, each taking for himself a share of names that benefit a person nothing in his religion, such as Judaism, Christianity and Zoroastrianism; or whose faith is not perfected by them, by taking some part of the Sharia and making it his religion while leaving aside its like or what is better than it, as is the state of the factions among the people of innovation (bid'ah), misguidance and those who divide the Ummah. For this reason He said: ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 6, verses 161–165:

{161} Allah commands His Prophet (ﷺ) to say and proclaim that he is upon guidance to the straight path (al-sirat al-mustaqim), the moderate religion (al-din al-mu'tadil), which includes beneficial beliefs, righteous deeds, the enjoining of every good and the forbidding of every evil. It is the upright religion (al-din al-hanif), inclining away from every crooked religion of the people of deviation, such as the Jews, the Christians and the polytheists. This is a general statement.

{162} Then he specified from this the most noble of the acts of worship, saying: ﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer and my sacrifice﴾; i.e., my slaughtering (dhabhi). This is because of the nobility and excellence of these two acts of worship, and because they indicate love of Allah, sincerity of religion toward Him, and drawing near to Him with the heart, the tongue and the limbs, and with the slaughter, which is the giving up of what the soul loves of wealth for what is more beloved to it, namely Allah, the Exalted. Whoever is sincere in his prayer and his sacrifice necessarily has sincerity toward Allah in all his other deeds. And His saying: ﴿and my living and my dying﴾; i.e., what I undertake in my life, what Allah makes flow upon me, and what He decrees for me in my death; all of it is ﴿for Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾.

{163} ﴿No partner has He﴾: in worship, just as He has no partner in dominion and governance. This sincerity toward Allah is not an innovation (ibtida') from me or a novelty (bid'ah) that I have brought from my own self; rather ﴿with that I have been commanded﴾, a binding command, and I do not get free of the obligation except by complying with it. ﴿And I am the first of the Muslims﴾: of this Ummah.

{164} ﴿Say: Shall I seek other than Allah﴾: among the created beings ﴿as a lord?﴾; i.e., would that be fitting, and would it be proper for me to take other than Him as a lord and manager? Allah is the Lord of everything; all creation falls under His lordship and submits to His command. Therefore it is obligatory upon me and upon others to take Allah as Lord, to be content with Him, and not to attach oneself to any of the lordly-dependent, poor and powerless beings. Then He encouraged and warned with this recompense, saying: ﴿And every soul earns only against itself﴾: of good and evil. ﴿And no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another﴾: rather, each one bears the burden of his own self, even if someone has been a cause of the misguidance of another and his burden; for upon him is the burden of causing it, without diminishing anything from the burden of the one who actually committed it. ﴿Then to your Lord is your return﴾: on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿and He will inform you of that over which you used to differ﴾: of good and evil, and will recompense you for that with the most complete recompense.

{165} ﴿And it is He who made you successors upon the earth﴾; i.e., some of you succeed others, and Allah has made you successors in the earth, subjected to you all that is in it, and tested you to see how you will act. ﴿And He raised some of you above others in degrees﴾: in strength, well-being, provision, form and character; ﴿that He may try you in what He has given you﴾: so your deeds differ. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment﴾: toward whoever disobeys Him and denies His signs, ﴿and indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: toward whoever believes in Him, does righteous deeds, and repents from the destructive sins.

End of the commentary on Surat al-An'am.
So to Allah belongs all praise and thanks. May Allah's blessings and peace be upon Muhammad, his family and companions, abundantly, until the Day of Judgment.
